title: The Arlo camera is a great product for keeping track of what goes on in ...
text:
I bought the Arlo camera a few months ago to keep an eye on our front porch and backyard, and it has exceeded my expectations in reliability and ease of use. Setup was straightforward — the app walked me through each step and the camera connected to Wi‑Fi without any hiccups. The video quality is clear, even at night; the night vision picks up people and packages well enough that I can easily make out faces and details.

Motion detection is accurate and customizable. I adjusted the sensitivity and activity zones so I only get alerts for meaningful events, which has cut down on false alarms from passing cars and trees. Alerts arrive quickly and I can view live footage or recorded clips instantly. The battery life is impressive; on our outdoor mounting it lasts weeks between charges, and swapping the rechargeable battery is simple.

Build quality feels solid and weatherproof. I also appreciate the cloud storage options and the ability to download clips when needed. Overall, the Arlo camera gives me peace of mind, excellent image quality, and dependable performance. Highly recommend for anyone wanting a reliable home security camera.

title: They went through the freaking washing machine.
text:
I bought these after a friend recommended them, expecting the usual “handle with care” warnings. I can honestly say: they survived a full washer and dryer cycle and came out looking and working like nothing happened. I’m still a bit in disbelief.

I wore them one afternoon, forgot they were in my jacket pocket, and ran my laundry like any other load. Forty-five minutes later I pulled them out, expecting to find a ruined mess. Instead they were damp, slightly wrinkled, and completely intact. The sound quality didn’t change, the buttons and connectors all functioned, and there was no weird buzzing or static. After letting them air dry for a few hours they were as good as new.

Build quality is surprisingly solid — the casing didn’t crack, and seams held up. They’re lightweight and comfortable, so I use them daily for calls and music. Battery life has been consistent with the product specs; no sudden drains or charging issues after the wash incident. Customer support was responsive when I emailed about care tips before my laundry mishap (yes, I felt sheepish), and they gave practical advice that matched my experience.

If you’re clumsy like me or have small pockets that eat earbuds, these are a great buy. I won’t deliberately put them through the washer again, obviously, but it’s incredibly reassuring to know they can survive that kind of accidental abuse. Highly recommend for anyone who needs reliable, durable earbuds that can handle real life.

title: OK
text:
I bought this OK fitness tracker a few weeks ago after reading some mixed reviews and wanting something affordable to monitor steps and sleep. Overall I’m moderately satisfied — it does many things adequately but nothing outstanding.

Setup was straightforward and the companion app is simple to navigate, though a bit slow to sync at times. Step counting seems reasonably accurate for daily walks, but it occasionally misses short indoor steps or counts arm movements as steps when I’m doing dishes. Heart rate monitoring works well during steady-state cardio but lags during interval workouts and sometimes shows spikes that don’t match how I feel.

Battery life met the advertised claim; I got about five days between charges with regular use and notifications enabled. The band is comfortable enough for everyday wear and the display is readable in daylight, though a bit dim indoors at the lowest setting.

I appreciate the sleep-tracking feature, but the sleep stages feel approximate and sometimes label restless nights inaccurately. Customer support responded politely when I had a sync issue, but resolution took a few days.

If you want a budget-friendly tracker with basic features, this is fine. If you need highly accurate metrics for serious training, consider a step up.

title: Disappointing
text:
I wanted to like this book — the premise sounded promising and the cover copy promised an engaging, fresh perspective — but overall it left me frustrated and underwhelmed. I’m giving it two stars because there are moments where the author’s insight shines through, but those are too few and too inconsistent to recommend this to most readers.

The pacing felt uneven from the start. The opening chapters dragged with excessive background detail that didn’t seem to serve the plot or character development, while later sections rushed through significant events as if the author realized halfway through that there wasn’t enough space. Important relationships and motivations were sketched rather than fully developed, so when the story demanded emotional payoff, I found myself uninvested.

Characterization was another weak spot. A few characters have distinct, memorable traits, but many felt like archetypes or plot devices. Dialogue frequently reads as stilted or expository; it tells rather than shows. I appreciate books that trust the reader to make connections, but here the opposite was true — the narration sometimes over-explains, which made the prose feel clunky.

On the positive side, the writing style is competent and there are flashes of genuinely good sentences and observations. A subplot about the protagonist’s past had potential and did deliver a handful of poignant moments. The book also wrapped up with a satisfying, if predictable, conclusion that ties most loose ends.

If you’re a completist fan of the author you might find value here, and readers who enjoy leisurely reads may appreciate the detailed descriptions. For me, though, the uneven pacing, thin character development, and occasional clumsy exposition made this a disappointing read that I can’t wholeheartedly recommend.

Alina writes such heartwarming stories to make you fall in love. The town of Felt has the most charming characters. Ally and Connor have been friends for a while because Connor is Ally’s brother’s best friend. They have both fought off their feelings for each other for years, but you can only hold down something so strong for so long.

Ally’s ex left her hurt and feeling like she wasn’t enough and alone with her twin girls. To prove to herself that she is enough, she does everything herself and doesn’t ask anyone for help. Connor has a tragic past with an ex which still haunts him and he has lingering feelings that he brings too much pain to the lives of those he loves.

Ally and Connor have to fight hard to be together and to get on the same page. Everytime one person was all in, the other tried backing away and vice versa. Together they are fire and I loved it. Connor is a good man, he is very sweet and treats Ally like a queen. And the way he treats Ally’s girls is just so wonderful it makes me so happy to see them together, his Peanut Brittle.

Ally and Connor’s HEA was worth the fight and the epilogues at the end wrapped up their story perfectly.

title: "original work of art" a tad too generous
text: When a book is released around the time of an author's death the literary world seems to shower him/her with an insane amount of praise that one has to wonder if death didn't come calling would would this book be so highly praised.  This is a short book (only about 244 pages which is slightly misleading because of page margins and text size this book is much shorter).  It's plot is compelling and it is wonderfully descriptive.  I found  Matthiessen' s tendency to switch between writing from the point of view of the main character to casual observer confusing and wish he would have stuck to one or the other.  The main character's purpose for being in this place and time (when you finally learn why)  is a great and equally tragic story line and by itself is enough to carry the reader.  The introduction of all minor characters just dilutes the story and introduces a bunch of characters that we don't care about and have absolutely no reason to care about.  Overall I gave this book 3 stars simply because the cast of characters and their relationship to the story is unmoving and distracting from the good aspects of this book.  It would be silly to tell someone not to read this book because the reality is, this is such a short book that even if you hated it you're not investing a huge chunk of your time.  It's not like reading a 1,000 page epic like PILLARS OF THE EARTH where if you hate it or get bored you've still got hundreds of pages to get through before you can properly decide what you're overall opinion is.

title: Great gift for puzzlers and interesting for non-puzzlers as well
text:
What makes this collection unique: it's printed on full-size newspaper stock
What makes this really amazing: they have taken the actual page from the newspaper of that year and reprinted it here with the ads and other articles as originally in the newspaper. You may find yourself ignoring the crossword and reading, say, the movie or book review from 1990. Or just perusing the ads.

The editors have taken one puzzle from each year back to 1942 and printed its entire page.

The downside to the book so far (I started at 2016 and worked backwards) is when you get to the Eugene Maleska years (77-93) (Oh, let me
correct myself: it's Eugene T. Maleska, not to be confused with all those other Eugene Maleska's in the USA). That "T" might tell you all you
need to know about his puzzles. They reek of what passed for knowledge way back when: obscure Broadway shows, "great" writers that most
people have never heard of, French language (by the way, there was an error in one of those), capitols of regions of small nations etc.

I have another compilation of NY Times puzzles that goes back decades which is very challenging because what passed for common knowledge back then is obscure now. However, that's not my issue with Maleska.

Altogether, this is a great gift for any crossword puzzler; mine was a gift as well.

title: Brlliant, funny, and even a bit disturbing
text:
"Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend" is McCay's overlooked masterpiece. "Little Nemo" gets all the press (and it deserves the highest possible praise) but The Fiend is often equally compelling. More adult in subject matter than Nemo, it is less visually resplendant, but still quite powerful in its invocation of the fears and hopes underlying our day-to-day thoughts.

This collection is the standard, but it collects only a fraction of what McCay produced (this is a reprint of a 1905 volume, but the strip ran until 1910 or 1911). You can pick up the Checker "Early Works" volumes for a more complete run (in questionable quality) and there are more strips in the Canemaker book on McCay as well as the Fantagraphics "Daydreams and Nightmares" (which I highly recommend).

Checker has since produced a fine collection: [[ASIN:1933160659 The Saturdays]] which would make a great follow-up to this book.

When I first wrote this review in 2006, I pleaded for someone to do this strip justice with a comprehensive reprint. Little did I know that Ulrich Merkl was, in fact, working on one at the time. You can search the web for his "The Complete Dream of the Rarebit Fiend" ([...]). I highly reccommend it, though it is a bit pricey. Amazon now lists it here: [[ASIN:3000207511 The Complete Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend]]

title: Child of Thorn and Hunger
text:
Note: I have read the story on RoyalRoad, which goes beyond the currently published books. This review stands as a synopsis of what I have read so far.

Fantastic story heavily inspired by Vampire: The Masquerade, showcasing the unnatural dominion of vampires over humans and most other magical creatures. This includes the existence of distinct vampire clans with unique supernatural traits and an inveterate hierarchical vampire society to maintain power and secrecy.

As the main character, Ariane is painfully reborn into a warrior bloodline with an antediluvian psychopath for a progenitor. Abandoned and left to fend for herself, she must navigate the perils of vampire society as an outcast and the lawless American frontier as a woman. As much potential as she has as a vampire, her beginnings leave her weak and at the mercy of far more powerful forces. It is with intelligence and true grit that she must learn to survive and thrive.

But the real struggle for Ariane is to maintain her sense of honor and humanity as she fights against the demands of her nature and the madness of her bloodline. While far from a warrior of light, she is fearless when she chooses to fight for what she believes in and builds bonds of deep friendship with interesting and diverse people. Her acts of kindness are rare, but they shine as genuine and without the avarice and cruelty inherent to her kind.

While she definitely stumbles at times, Ariane remains steadfast to her friends and an anti-hero to those she saves along the way. I hope that her journey keeps her from succumbing to wickedness and allows her to emerge as something special. A dark star in a world of darkness.

title: Cute but not purposeful
text:
I bought this because the photos made it look charming and the size seemed perfect for a small corner by my sink. After using it for a few weeks I’m giving it three stars — it’s cute and well made in a decorative way, but it falls short as a genuinely useful kitchen item.

First the positives: the finish is attractive and matches the description. The paint/print hasn’t faded and there are no noticeable chips or defects out of the box. It feels reasonably sturdy for a decorative piece and the seams are neat. If your primary goal is to add a bit of personality to a windowsill, open shelf, or to complement a farmhouse/retro vibe, this will do that job fine. I also appreciate that it arrived carefully packaged; no scratches or scuffs.

Now the drawbacks that keep me from giving it more stars. The product is marketed as being functional for holding sponges/soap, but in practice it doesn’t drain well (if it’s designed to). Water collects in the bottom and even after draining a sponge for a while it still leaves a damp puddle. That makes the sponge stay wet and feel slimy after a few days — I’ve had to empty and dry it regularly, which defeats the point of a “hands-free” holder. If you use it for soap, the soap can end up sitting in a little pool and becoming mushy faster than I expected.

The size description was slightly misleading: it’s smaller than I pictured. It fits one compact sponge or a small bar of soap, but not much else. If you hoped to store multiple items (brush + sponge + scrubber), you’ll be disappointed. Also, there’s no non-slip base, so it slides on my counter when I grab the sponge unless I keep it on a textured tray.

In summary: attractive and decent quality for decoration, but not very practical for continuous everyday use unless you don’t mind occasional maintenance (emptying and drying). I’m keeping it because it brightens up the area, but if you need something primarily functional to keep sponges dry and neat, look for a holder specifically designed with drainage and non-slip features. This one is more about style than substance.

title: Should Be a Movie
text:
I picked up Should Be a Movie because the premise — a story so cinematic it feels like a screenplay waiting to happen — sounded irresistible, and for the most part the book delivers exactly that kind of experience. From the opening chapter I was immediately swept into lush, vividly described scenes that felt staged for a wide-screen adaptation: sweeping locations, sharp, witty dialogue, and a cast of characters who are equal parts charming and flawed.

The narrator’s voice is one of the book’s biggest strengths. There’s a self-aware, slightly sardonic tone that kept me smiling aloud on the subway and turning pages faster than I meant to. The protagonist is likable without being perfect; their internal monologue balances humor with genuine vulnerability, which made it easy to root for them even when their choices were messy. Secondary characters are well-drawn and memorable — a friend who steals every scene with deadpan one-liners, a love interest with complicated motives, and a rival who’s both infuriating and oddly relatable.

Pacing is generally strong. The middle section unspooled like a montage: set-ups, missteps, reconciliations, and a few surprises that kept me engaged. There are moments of quiet reflection that add emotional depth, and then the narrative will snap back into high-energy sequences that feel cinematic in the best way. The author’s knack for visual detail makes many scenes pop — I could see the city lights, hear the background music, and almost feel the weather on the characters’ skin.

That said, the book isn’t flawless. A couple of plot threads felt a bit underdeveloped, leaving me wanting more explanation about certain character motivations. And the ending, while satisfying, leans a little towards neatness; I would have enjoyed a touch more ambiguity or risk. A few sentences occasionally veered into purple prose, breaking the otherwise crisp rhythm, but those instances were infrequent.

Overall, Should Be a Movie is an entertaining, well-written read that will particularly delight anyone who loves contemporary fiction with strong dialogue and cinematic flair. It’s the kind of book you’ll want to recommend to friends and — yes — imagine being adapted for the screen. I’m giving it four stars because it’s consistently enjoyable and emotionally engaging, even if a little tightening in places would have made it exceptional.

title: One of the best purchases I've made!
text: I am an avid hobby photography enthusiast, but I prefer to focus on creativity rather than technical application. I'm also a small person with a bad shoulder so I can't really carry around heavy equipment. My favorite subject is historic architecture especially decorative architectural details. I'm so happy that I chose this out of all the others in the travel camera category of similar quality and price. Selecting the best camera to take on my trip to Europe was a serious mission for me and I chose this Pentax after thoroughly researching reviews and specifications. It was a fortunate decision because I took 982 shots in 10 days in Vienna, most of them great and many just amazing for me at least. The image quality is excellent, the zoom power is incredible, and operation is easy and responsive. One thing that I especially like is how great the anti-shake feature is. I don't have the steadiest hands and that has often been a problem for me before, but I used this camera without even thinking much about it and as long as I took at least 3 shots at a time I always got at least one perfectly clear one. The only negative was that I wished I had bought an extra battery. Every daily excursion I took, I ran out of battery power towards the end. As I said I take a lot of pictures at a time, but I would have taken even more if I had taken an extra battery. I would definitely recommend this camera if you are particular about both the quality and ease of use.

title: Well Done Expose' On The Radical Right
text:
This book is part muckraking,part psyhcological analysis of the extreme right that has taken over the Republican Party.
Mr. Blumenthal did a large amount of research in this journalistic endeavor and he added a section at the end of the book to cover the first year of the Obama administration.

One Eisenhower quote that seldom gets mentioned is found in the Introduction, it's a warning and it's not about the military-industrial complex.
"His admonition to beware the danger posed to democracy by those who seek 'freedom from the necessity of informing themselves and making up their own minds concerning these tremendous complex ands difficult questions.'"
That is a tool used quite effectively by the conservative media apparatus.

One of the intriguing subjects in "Republican Gomorrah" was the discovery of Sarah Palin, who discovered her, how and what they did to promote her.
Another is the general history of the religious right on homosexuality and hypocrisy.
Contrasting the downfall of Larry Craig and Ted Haggard with conservatives like David Vitter and Newt Gingrich.
Added to the mix is the "kingmaker" that believes his endorsement is essential for any potential Republican presidential candidate.
Look too deeply into the conservative religious right and you see double-standards and lots of activity that runs counter to Scripture.
On page 42 the author writes "Under Reconstructionist rules of engagement, lying, deception, and stealth are considered legitimate tactics and are even encouraged."

This book is thoroughly documented and is a fast read. More important is what it exposes in the Republican Party and how that element wormed it's way in.
This is a fairly current work and one that every American voter should read.

title: Pretty great, but sometimes not tough enough
text:
I’ve been using this product for a few months now and overall I’m pretty happy with it. The design is attractive and fits nicely into my kitchen aesthetic; it feels well-made at first glance and the finish has held up to daily use without any obvious wear. It’s easy to clean and the parts that come into contact with food don’t retain smells, which I really appreciate. Assembly was straightforward and the instructions were clear.

Performance-wise, it does what it’s supposed to for most everyday tasks. I use it several times a week and it handles routine jobs without fuss. The controls are intuitive and I like that there are a few settings so I can tweak things depending on what I’m making. It’s also relatively quiet compared with some older models I’ve owned, which is a nice bonus during early morning prep.

That said, there have been a few moments where I wished it were a bit more heavy-duty. When I put it through more demanding tasks, it strains and seems like it’s pushing its limits — not unsafe, but noticeably slower and less effective than I expected. For heavy users or those who frequently work with tougher ingredients, this might be something to consider. A sturdier motor or reinforced components would make it perfect.

Customer support was responsive when I had a minor question, which was reassuring. Given the price point, I think it’s a good buy for most households — reliable for day-to-day use, attractive, and easy to maintain — but if you need industrial-level toughness, you may need to look elsewhere. Overall, I’d recommend it for average home use.

title: I love this blanket
text:
I bought this blanket on a whim during a chilly spring evening and it’s quickly become one of my favorite purchases for the house. The first thing I noticed when it arrived was the weight — it’s substantial without feeling heavy, which gives it a cozy, comforting drape. The fabric is incredibly soft against my skin; it doesn’t have that scratchy or rough feeling some cheaper throws do. I’ve used it on the couch for movie nights, draped over the end of the bed for an extra layer, and even taken it outside for a cool morning coffee. It handles all of those scenarios beautifully.

The color I chose matched the online photos very well and hasn’t faded after several washes. Speaking of laundry, the blanket went through the washer and dryer with no issues: no pilling, no shrinking, and it came out just as plush as the first day. The seams are well-stitched and I don’t expect any unraveling. It also repels pet hair better than I expected — my cat still sheds, but the hair brushes off easily and a quick lint roller does the rest.

It’s large enough to comfortably cover an adult when curled up but not so bulky that it takes over the whole couch. The warmth level is perfect for year-round use in my moderately heated home — cozy on cool nights, but breathable enough for spring and fall. Overall, this blanket has become my go-to for comfort and looks like it will last a long time. Very happy with the value and quality; I’d buy it again and would recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable, cozy throw.

title: Recommend This Switch Box
text:
After several month's use on my HD flat panel TV, I can easily recommend this box if you need to "fan-out" a single HDMI input port to five independent signal sources. It does exactly what it says -- you control which input is selected, without the box trying to automatically switch to whichever input line is "active". The remote works well and the overall hook-up and operation is simple and straight forward. Overall device quality seemed very good and packaging for shipment was good. I could not detect any added audio or HD video signal deterioration/distortion. The instructions are fairly adequate, just remember to pull the plastic insulating tape out of the back of the remote to allow the battery to make internal electrical contact to start the remote! This was not mentioned in the instruction sheet of the unit I received.

I can understand why some reviewers have complained that the power and selected channel indicator LED's are too bright and are distracting. My solution was to put a 3.5 inch strip of gray electrical tape across the front of the unit. The gray is less obtrusive than the white electrical tape that I tried, and does it a better job of taming the LED's output. You get a diffuse lighted dot to indicate "power on" and the channel that is "on", and can neatly write the name of the signal for the channels on it [e.g. DVD, Fire Stick, Computer, Game, etc.] with a Ultra Fine Point permanent marker pen. Put a 3.5 inch strip of Scotch Magic Mending Tape on top to protect what you have written on the electrical tape if that is a concern.

18December2016 update -- one of the white LED's that indicates the selected channel has failed, but otherwise unit continues to work fine.

title: Love it--a really fun read!
text:
I try really hard to not rehash the entire story or give a bunch of spoilers when I review a book, but it may be hard not to this time! I'll do my best, though. ;)

I received this book to rebiew from the Shut Up & Read group's Read It & Reap event. I have to say, I have been extremely fortunate in the books I've been given to review through them so far. There really haven't been any misses. :)

Anyway, about this book...

I admit it--halfway into the very first chapter I was convinced I was going to hate this book. Liora seemed like the typical, overly-angsty teenager often depicted in paranormal fantasy these days. I initially found her constant whiny and hating herself grating. All I can say is I'm so happy I read chapter 2!

Lucky kicks ass! There's really no other way to describe her. The demon half of Liora who takes over at night, separated from Liora by a curse, she is angry, obviously. And that anger is often turned toward Liora, her fully human side. She is also strong, practical, loyal to her friends, and more willing to look into herself and face the things that make her uncomfortable that she admits. And as time went by, I found Liora to be less annoying as she found her own strength and started to face her own inner "demons".

There are only a couple of things that prevented me from giving this book five stars. The first is that I felt like the romance between Keiran and Liora/Lucky felt too conveniently done to me. There didn't seem to be any build up to it at all. The second issue is that conversations sometimes felt stilted to me. While I appreciate that there was a distinct lack of inappropriate idioms throughout, the almost complete lack of contractions often made discussions feel too formal and unnatural.

This book had everything--romance, fear, growth, drama, excitement, sadness, and victory. It was a great story and I can't wait to read the next one!

title: A brief but entertaining chronicle
text:
I recently finished reading this little book about the Norman conquest of England almost a millenia ago. I found this book interesting, and well written. The author was a former British Naval officer, and he is obviously pro-British, which did not mater to me one way or another.
By genetics, I am part English, and completely Western European, and I read this book to better understand my people's history pre-America. I enjoyed Howarth's take on village life of the commoners/peasantry int he first chapter; he details their low stress, and deep sense of belonging and racial/English community. Written 40 years ago, in a story with no non-Whites, it was still acceptable to talk about racial/tribal community as a natural and healthy thing. It was Whites fighting and oppressing other Whites, and thus he could speak openly about tribal loyalty. Overall, it was a pretty good book.

1)See the future - where are you going with your team

2)Engage others and develop them - Assign the right people to the right jobs and help them to smooth out their rough edges.

3)Reinvent Continuously - Continue to learn

4)Value Results and Relationships - Get results from those in the right position by being relationships.

5)Embody Values - Walk the talk. Be a role model for what you believe in and your team will follow.

As Debbie learns, understands and implements Jeff's teaching she begins to see excellent results.

This book is a quick but powerful read. I highly recommend to new leaders.

title: Useless for techies
text:
I'm a developer building a company-internal website and I'm struggling to organize all the information it will contain. I bought this book hoping to ease that struggle. What I found is for a technical person like me, this book was so useless that it has compelled me to write my first Amazon review in years.

I planned to read it cover to cover. After 50 pages I realized that I haven't really read anything at all yet. So far it's been ridiculously verbose, rambling, and content-free. So I gave up and started skimming.

I couldn't find much better in the remaining pages. Page after page of touchy-feely gobbledygook that has not helped me organize information at all.

There are more useless diagrams in this book than I've ever seen before. For example, the term "synonym ring" is defined as a group of words with the same meaning. Does it really take a diagram with a bunch of arrows in a circle to explain that? (Figure 9-2)

To explain the concept of equivalence we have another diagram: "A=B" inside a circle. (Figure 9-21) Does such a diagram really enhance anybody's understanding of the concept of equivalence? Why does this diagram even exist in the first place?

Maybe some business or consultant type might get something out of this book. For a developer, run away. Fast.

If you’re on the fence, measure your space and go for it. It’s a tasteful, well-made decoration that elevates a room without feeling overdone. I’m very satisfied with this purchase and would buy from this seller again. Five stars.

I too have been having similar respiratory problems (since I had a second litter box near my bed to make sure the kitten didn't have any accidents at night).

He often had pink sand on his nose, so it's not a big leap that some of it was getting into his lungs.
Just wanted to warn everyone that this litter is not a good choice for kittens. I've switched both cat boxes to fresh step premium crystals, it's a larger, pearl like bb which has no dust and is too big to be inhaled! Hope this helps others whose kittens are short of breath.

title: Feels even better than it looks (and no problems in Linux)
text:
When another HTPC-style keyboard finally irritated me enough to replace it, I decided to try the diNovo Edge. In photos, the Edge looks attractive enough, but I always thought that the slimness made it look a little, well, flimsy. After actually getting it and trying it in person, (a) it looks even classier than the photos, and (b) it's got a nice heft and rigidity to it that gives it a feeling of quality I was not expecting. It really is a brushed aluminum piece there, not shiny plastic. Admittedly, it's expensive, but after trying it out I don't think it's disproportionately so.

About the trackpad ("TouchDisc"): I noticed some reviews commenting that it's nothing special. That's partially true; for the most part, it works just like normal laptop trackpad, which is good. The scrolling support has an interesting feature, though: on normal rectangular laptop trackpads, you place your finger at the right edge of the trackpad, and move it up and down to scroll. But you soon hit the top or bottom edge of the trackpad and have to stop. On the diNovo Edge you start the same way, by placing your finger at the right edge, but because it's round you instead move clockwise or counterclockwise to scroll, so you never have to stop. So once you start it scrolling you can just keep spinning your finger in circles around the outside edge over and over, pause, or change direction. The speed and accuracy of this approach are both big improvements, particularly when scrolling up and down long pages.

As for Linux support: no need for special drivers for the support of the main keys or the touchpad. In fact, many of the special media keys worked as expected out of the box, including the volume slider. Depending on what you're using to map keyboard shortcuts, though, not all of the media keys were available to be mapped without some tweaking. For these, a program called "keytouch" (probably available in most package managers) let me program the rest; it included settings for a different diNovo keyboard that seems to work fine for the Edge and includes most of those other keys already.

title: A Colorful Spectrum of Poetry and Painting
text:
Victoria Franks paints pictures with oil and with words, each complementing the other. Her book of poetry and art The Aroma of Coffee is colorful and sensual. From the mountains of South America and the deserts of Arizona to the swamps and shores of Northwest Florida, Franks details the unique beauty she perceives.
Her work covers the gamut of pride in country and despair at war and loneliness to passion, love, and joy. Her poetry shows us the simple yet difficult life of Columbians alongside the complexities of their struggle. Every topic she covers resounds with insightful truth.
Flavored with chocolate, potatoes and corn, mojitos and margaritas, the aroma of coffee is merely a tease. Her work is colored with every hue of the spectrum and accented with Spanish words that roll off the tongue as well as the page, their English definition less important than their fluidity.
Readers easily see the pictures of her words and infer the meanings just below the surface of her paintings. Franks travels effortlessly from one medium to the other and takes the reader with her.

title: you end up having to shuffle them yourself
text:
I bought this deck hoping it would be an easy, fun addition to family game nights, but I ended up deeply disappointed. The product description implies the cards come ready to use, with everything you need. What it doesn’t tell you is that the cards arrive in several identical partial stacks that are not shuffled together at all. So instead of popping it open and playing, I had to spread every single card out and manually shuffle them together to get a usable deck. That might sound petty, but it dramatically changes the experience—this is a toy meant for convenience and quick play, not a craft project in card organizing.

The printing quality is decent and the artwork is fine, but none of that matters when the basic functionality is broken. If you have kids, forget letting them handle this right away; I had to do the tedious sorting myself to avoid them seeing duplicate groups in a row. It took me 20–30 minutes to mix the stacks properly so the game didn’t feel repetitive. I also noticed a few cards that looked slightly bent from being tightly stacked, which wouldn’t happen with a properly randomized deck.

Customer service wasn’t helpful when I reached out—their response was generic and essentially shrugged that some people prefer to shuffle themselves. That’s not the point. The product should arrive ready to play. For the price, I expected better packaging and quality control. If you’re okay spending extra time prepping the deck for play, maybe it will work for you. But if you want something you can open and use immediately, don’t buy this. I’ll be returning mine if I can. One star.

text: This has to be one of the sweetest "morbid" stories ever told - the perfect Morbid Valentine for your beloved. Carl von Cosel was a German x-ray technician living in Florida who fell in love with one of his Tuberculosis patients - a beautiful young woman named Elena. Carl believed that Elena was destined to be his wife and he was overcome with despair when she finally succumbed to her illness. He decided that even death could not keep them apart, and he exhumed his bride and brought her body back to his home, where he cleaned it up and used an elaborate embalming process to preserve her remains. He kept her there with him for 8 years, during which time she naturally began to fall apart a bit, but Carl kept her looking as good as possible by filling in her sunken features with wax. He even inserted a tube in her vaginal canal so they could consummate their love. Yes, it doesn't get much sicker than this! But strangely enough, when Carl was eventually arrested, most women of the time (1920's-30's) thought it was a very romantic story and did not think poorly of the old man at all. Isn't that sweet?

text: My wife and I took these out for the first time this weekend.  I only configured it for rider/passenger because all the modes it supports struck me just a little too busy at first.  I may add music later (maybe) but I just don't need to take calls that can't wait till my next stop.  Now I have a few issues with this unit.  At first we tried opening a connection only when we wanted to talk.  It would connect so I could hear her, or she could hear me but not both.  We'd pull over and fiddle with it (on/off, connect/disconnect) then we'd get it working, so off we'd go.  But then next time we wanted to connect it would fail again.  After about thee times we decided to leave it open/connected.  Problem with that is it's transmitting engine noise and everything else the whole time.  Modulating the volume below about 3/4 results in faint garbled transmissions, not simple volume reduction.  The beep tones it issues, on/off, connect/disconnect, etc. are violently loud at any volume setting.  On my VTX1300 (v-twin) anything above 40 mph is too loud to practically use the unit even at max volume.  Now, I'm not blaming the unit for the noisy bike, but this is a factor to consider if you're buying.  You'll notice I still rated it 4 of 5 because it does what it claims and the overall convenience, feature set and price point beats anything else out there.  I also still hope to resolve the connection issue; I'm going to review the manual and play with it some more on the chance that I missed something with the operation - I'll update the review if I find anything.

title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought Flyover Nation out of curiosity and finished it in two sittings — surprised, moved, and a little ashamed that I’d underestimated what a “travel through America” book could do. The author doesn’t romanticize or caricature; instead, he listens. The portraits of small towns, factory floors, church basements, and open highways are honest and granular, full of people whose stories stay with you. What I appreciated most was the balance: empathy without sentimentality, critique without condescension. The writing is clear and often quietly lyrical, making the book both informative and emotionally resonant.

As someone who grew up in the Midwest but has lived in cities for years, this felt like a necessary reminder of the complexity and dignity of places often dismissed as “flyover.” It also challenged some of my assumptions and opened new ones. Thought-provoking, humane, and beautifully observed — a book I’ll recommend and return to.

title: Filled My Soul
text:
I rarely write reviews, but Filled My Soul moved me enough that I had to share. I bought this book during a time when life felt noisier and more hurried than I wanted, and it turned out to be exactly what I didn’t know I was looking for.

The writing is intimate without being indulgent; the author speaks with a warmth that feels like a conversation with a wise friend. Each chapter offered small, practical reflections that were easy to read but lingered long after I closed the book. I found myself pausing to journal, to try a suggested practice, or simply to sit in quiet appreciation. Those simple exercises slowly added up to a noticeable shift in how I approached my days.

What I appreciated most was the balance between insight and accessibility. This isn’t preachy self-help jargon — it’s grounded, humble guidance that respects where you are while gently nudging you toward more meaning and presence. The anecdotes felt real, not staged, and the author’s humility made the lessons feel attainable.

The book’s pacing was perfect; I could read a chapter in one sitting or savor it over several days. The physical copy I received was well-produced, with pleasant typography and a durable cover.

If you’re looking for a book that offers gentle clarity and practical tools for cultivating a deeper, calmer life, Filled My Soul is a lovely companion. I’ll be returning to passages again and recommending it to friends.

title: Be careful what you ask for
text:
I got this book because I heard the author and her husband interviewed recently on NPR. Based on that, I thought "Wondering Who You Are" would be a uniquely uplifting story. I expected something along the lines of Jill Bolte Taylor's "My Stroke of Insight," which was a fascinating and inspiring first-hand account of a young woman's stroke and rehabilitation. For sure, this book did keep me on the edge of my seat - I couldn't put it down (as other reviewers have noted). And it did have some engaging parts, like the description of Richard's chaotic hospitalization, the couple's experience with a mediator over the legal settlement, and Lea's sexual exploration, among others. But I came away from the book feeling it was over-wrought and just plain sad. Here is a woman (the author) who actually leads a rich, surprising, adventure-filled life, but she just can't stop weeping over her lack of self-fulfillment. It's ironic that she spends so much of the book bemoaning the loss of her remarkable husband's pre-surgery personality, and yet while she had him that way, she was an alcoholic who preferred to be out partying rather than staying home with him and her children! Clearly she is transformed by her experience with him after he loses his personality, but she seems to find barely an ounce of delight in any of his rehabilitation successes or her own exploration of the wondrous possibilities life has to offer. Instead we hear too many times about her tears.

If nothing else, what this book teaches is - be careful what you ask for. If you long for unconditional love and acceptance, here is post-surgery Richard, able to offer these things in spades…. but it's creepy. Gurus like Byron Katie teach us the joy of living in the moment and questioning our personal narratives, but those approaches to self-transformation are only viable if we have a memory and a life story - as Richard does not.

text:
I bought this raised bowl for my pug because our vet recommended we try a shallower, elevated dish to make eating more comfortable for his flat face and to reduce gulping. The product does what it says — the height is just right for him, and he seems to strain his neck less when reaching the kibble. It also appears to help him slow down a little, which is a small win.

That said, there are several things that kept me from giving five stars. The non-slip base works only on clean floors; if there’s any dust or kibble crumbs it slides a bit, and on our hardwood it moved when he pawed around. The plastic feels thinner than I expected and has picked up light scratches from washing after just a few uses. Also, the bowl depth is fine for dry kibble but not ideal for wet food or for adding water — things slosh more easily at this shallow depth.

Overall, it’s a useful, no-frills product that meets the basic need and my dog did adjust to it quickly. If you want a lightweight, affordable elevated bowl for a brachycephalic pup, this is okay, but don’t expect premium materials or a miracle for mess control.

title: Sheds like other goat hair brushes, but great value

I’ve been using this goat hair makeup brush for a few weeks now, and for the price it’s a solid find. It picks up powder and blush nicely and blends product out to a natural, airbrushed finish. For everyday use it performs well.

It’s not a dense buffing brush for heavy cream products, but that’s not what I bought it for.

Overall, I’m happy with this purchase. Performance is very good for the price, and while the shedding is a downside, it’s consistent with other natural goat-hair brushes I’ve owned. If you want an affordable, soft brush for powders and blending, this one delivers great value. I’d recommend it with the caveat that you should handle it gently and expect a bit of shedding initially.

title: Too many contradictions - sometimes on adjoining pages
text:
I wanted to like this book, despite having read O'Reilly's "Killing Patton" which contained a very thin conspiracy theory about Patton's death. "Legends and Lies" purports to be a history book but is filled with inconsistencies and inaccuracies.

For example, on page 5, the book states that "Daniel Boone was born in Pennsylvania in 1734, the sixth child of ...". Yet on page 6, in a photo apparently depicting an unidentified stone house, the cut says "... Daniel Boone was the seventh of twelve children." Which is it?

On page 67, the narrative talks about Kit Carson being attacked by a band of Kiowa Indians on November 25, 1864. "Within hours, about fourteen hundred warriors attacked. It was similar to the situation in which General Custer would find himself a few months later." But 'Custer's Last Stand' occurred on June 25, 1876, nearly twelve YEARS later, not 'a few months.'

Also on page 67, "... while the Navajos, after signing a treaty in 1868 with General Sherman, were moved to a portion of their traditional lands, where they have remained." But on the photo on the facing page, the cutline says the Navajos "...settled peacefully on this land, as negotiated by (Kit) Carson." But in 1868, Carson was in Colorado, either dead or dying, according to the same chapter.

While any history book might understandably contain discrepencies, when compared to other history books, it should not contradict itself, especially on adjoining pages. For that reason, I stopped reading this book about half-way through and consider it a waste of money.

text:

Installation was simple — plug the USB end into the TV’s USB port and plug the Ethernet cable into the adapter. The TV immediately recognized the connection without any fuss. No extra drivers, no fiddling through menus beyond selecting “Wired” instead of Wi‑Fi. Once connected, my TV showed a solid wired connection and streaming apps opened noticeably faster.

Performance-wise, it’s rock solid. 4K streaming on Netflix and Amazon Prime plays smoothly with no buffering, and online gaming feels much more responsive. I ran a speed test through the TV and the results were consistent with what I get on my wired laptop. The adapter stays cool to the touch, and I haven’t seen any disconnects after several weeks of daily use.

Build quality seems good — the connector feels sturdy and the cable is a decent thickness (not flimsy). It’s unobtrusive and doesn’t add much bulk behind the TV. My only minor gripe is that it makes the single USB port occupied, but that’s a small trade-off for reliable Ethernet.

If you have an Insignia Roku TV and need a dependable wired connection, this adapter works exactly as advertised. Finally, a wired solution that actually works with my TV — very happy with this purchase.

title: Won't fit in anything less than a 29" doorway
text:
I bought this pet gate hoping it would solve my problem of keeping my dog out of the kitchen. The build quality is solid — heavy-duty metal, good welds, and a powder-coated finish that looks like it will hold up to scratches and rust. The latching mechanism is sturdy and easy to operate with one hand, which is great when you're carrying groceries. The gate also swings open both ways and has a decent pressure-fit system that felt secure once installed.

That said, the biggest downside for me is the advertised doorway size. It really doesn’t work in anything smaller than a 29" opening. I have a standard interior doorway that measures 28" and even with the rubber pads and a tiny bit of flex, the gate wouldn't seat properly and left a noticeable gap at the top. I had to return it because I couldn't make it safe for my dog. If your doorway is 29" or wider, you'll probably be very happy with this gate. But if you have narrower openings, check the dimensions carefully — the seller could be clearer about that requirement. Overall, well-made and functional, just too large for many typical doorways. I’d give it four stars because it performs well when it fits.

This is not an easy puzzle -- it's not impossible but it's trickier than other 1000-piece puzzles I've worked. But with patience and careful pattern matching, you'll get there! I really enjoyed working it over about 3 days (off and on) between household chores/etc.

The colors are vibrant, and the pieces are thick enough to take some minor abuse. The photo on the box provides a guide, and the pieces are marked on the back with letters that allow you to "group" them together to make placement a little easier.

I definitely enjoyed putting this one together, and it's sparked my interest in trying more puzzles at home. After all, my next cruise isn't for another 4 months!

I bought this helmet for weekend LARP events and medieval reenactments and it has exceeded my expectations in every way. The chin strap is sturdy and easy to adjust one-handed, which is handy when I’m suiting up quickly. The helmet sits securely even during running and shield bashing; I never felt it shift or loosen.

Durability appears excellent — I’ve had a few decent impacts from foam weapons and some accidental drops, and the helmet has only picked up a few scuffs that add character. No cracks or structural issues. Cleaning is simple: a quick wipe with a damp cloth removes dirt and sweat stains without affecting the finish.

Sizing was accurate based on the manufacturer’s chart; I double-checked my measurements and ordered the recommended size and it fits perfectly. Shipping was fast and packaging prevented any dings in transit.

Overall this helmet gives a great balance of authenticity, comfort, and durability for LARP use. It looks great in photos, feels secure during play, and stands up to rough handling. I’d recommend it to anyone wanting a convincing, functional helmet without the cost and weight of real metal armor.

title: Nice Cabinet and Board, BAD Darts
text:
I bought this dart cabinet and board set a few weeks ago because I wanted a neat, all-in-one option for occasional games in the garage. First impressions were positive: the cabinet itself looks good, is solidly built, and the magnetic closures keep it tidy when not in use. The finish is nice and it mounted easily to the wall — overall it gives a more polished look than a cheap foam board hung with screws.

Unfortunately, the darts and the board are where this product falls apart. The board surface is a cheap sisal substitute that wears unevenly and already shows fraying around the triple 20 after only a handful of sessions. More noticeably, the included darts feel very low quality. The shafts are flimsy plastic that bent or loosened almost every game, and the threads that attach to the flights stripped easily. I tried tightening them and replacing flights, but they didn’t hold alignment and the darts wobbled a lot in flight, which made accurate throws nearly impossible.

The scoring ring on the board is thin metal and seems okay for stopping bounce-outs, but the combination of soft board material and poor darts resulted in a higher-than-expected rate of bounced or dropped darts — not fun when you’re keeping score. I would have been happier if the set included at least mid-range darts or allowed for easy upgrades; swapping in better darts helps, but doesn’t solve the fact that the board itself degrades quickly.

If you want a sharp-looking cabinet and a basic board for casual display and very light play, this will do the job. If you’re buying it to play regularly or expect decent dart performance out of the box, you’ll be disappointed and likely need to buy replacement darts (and possibly a better board) soon after. Hence the middle-of-the-road rating.

text:
I bought this padel racket after reading a few budget-friendly recommendations and having only played a handful of times before. For the price, it’s really well made — the finish looks clean, the handle feels solid, and the weight distribution is comfortable for my swing. I’ve played about a dozen matches with it now and it has held up well: no chips or visible wear on the face, and the grip hasn’t loosened or torn. It’s responsive and gives a good balance between control and power, which has helped me improve my volleys and serves.

That said, there are a couple of things to be aware of. First, the racket is a bit stiffer than I expected, so if you’re used to very flexible frames you might notice less forgiveness on off-center hits. It’s not a dealbreaker, but it did take a few sessions to adjust. Second, the included cover is pretty thin — it protects from dust but won’t do much for accidental drops or if you toss it into a crowded car trunk with other gear. I bought a padded case separately.

Overall I’m happy with this purchase. It offers excellent value: sturdy construction, pleasant feel, and solid performance for recreational players and intermediate hobbyists. If you want pro-level specs or top-tier shock absorption, look higher up the price range, but for casual play this is a smart pick.

title: Needed wheels
text:
I bought these replacement wheels because the original set on my cat’s rolling carrier started to squeak and wobble after a few years of use. I’d been putting off replacing them, but my carrier wouldn’t roll smoothly anymore and I was tired of careful maneuvering whenever I took my cat to the vet. Overall, these wheels did what I needed — so I’m giving four stars.

First, the fit was the most important part for me, and these matched the measurements listed in the description. Installation was straightforward: a little pop and snap into the socket, no tools required for the front caster wheels. The rear wheels needed a small screwdriver to remove a clip from the old set, but the package included clear instructions and a tiny plastic washer that made everything sit snugly. After swapping all four, the carrier rolled much more smoothly and quietly. No more loud scraping on tile or the awkward lurch when turning.

The materials feel decent for the price. The plastic is not super heavy-duty, but it’s sturdier than the flimsy wheels I had on the original carrier toward the end. They’ve handled a few months of regular use (weekly trips to the vet and occasional travel) without cracking or excessive wear. The bearings are adequate — not silky-smooth like higher-end casters, but good enough for a pet carrier that’s mostly moved short distances by hand.

That said, there are a couple of reasons I didn’t give five stars. One wheel arrived with a slight cosmetic scuff, and the axle housing on one piece felt a little looser than the others — it’s still worked fine but it gave me a moment of concern during installation. Also, the wheels don’t swivel quite as freely as the originals did, so turning on thick carpet still requires a bit of effort. If you have heavy or very active pets, or plan to pull the carrier over long distances, you might prefer a metal-bearing wheel or a branded replacement.

In summary: these wheels are a solid, affordable fix that saved me from buying a whole new carrier. They fit well, were easy to install, and restored smooth, quiet rolling for everyday use. A small quality-control improvement would make them perfect, but for the price they’re a practical and satisfactory replacement.

title: Items missing :(
text:
I don’t usually write reviews, but I felt I had to after this disappointing purchase. I bought this set for my seven-year-old’s birthday because the pictures and description made it look like a complete kit with everything needed to build multiple models. What arrived was missing several key pieces, and the whole experience felt like a bait-and-switch.

Right out of the box I noticed the box felt lighter than I expected. We opened it together and started sorting parts, following the instructions included. About 20 minutes in we hit a wall: essential connector pieces and what should have been one of the motor assemblies were nowhere to be found. I checked every compartment and bag multiple times, double-checked the parts list in the manual, and even dumped everything out onto the carpet to be certain. Several unique, identifiable parts that are shown in the product photos and listed as included were absent.

Customer service was not much help. I reached out via the seller’s contact page and got an automated confirmation immediately, but then silence for days. A week later I received a generic reply asking for photos and order information, which I supplied. After that, no follow-up and no resolution. I tried again to escalate through Amazon, and while they eventually offered a partial refund or a return for a full refund, it was cumbersome: I would have had to box everything back up, ship it off, and wait weeks. By then my child’s party had passed and the toy lost its purpose.

The product that did arrive looks well-made and the parts we did have seem sturdy and engaging, so I can only judge based on what was actually delivered. For the price, I expected a complete set. Missing parts render the kit unusable for the builds shown in the instructions, which was the whole point of buying it.

If you’re considering this for a gift or a project with a deadline, beware: there’s a real chance this will show up incomplete and it appears the seller may not be responsive. I’m giving one star because the product as received failed to meet basic expectations and customer service didn’t resolve the issue in any timely or satisfactory way.

text:
I bought "More Lets Sticker and Paste" for my 5-year-old after she loved the original edition, and it has quickly become a favorite activity book in our house. The variety of stickers and the simple paste exercises are just right for her age — not too easy that she gets bored, and not too complex that she gets frustrated. The pages are durable enough to withstand enthusiastic little hands, and the stickers stick well but are still easy for her to peel off herself, which is a big win for her independence.

What I appreciate most is how this book balances fun with learning. There are matching activities, simple storytelling prompts where she adds stickers to complete scenes, and basic fine-motor tasks that subtly reinforce hand-eye coordination and attention to detail. I’ve noticed she’s more confident with scissors and glue after using this book alongside supervised craft time.

The artwork is bright and engaging without being overwhelming. Characters and scenes are varied, which keeps each page feeling fresh. Some stickers are reusable if you’re gentle, which has extended the play value beyond a single session. We’ve used several pages as part of rainy-day crafts and also taken a few on car trips to keep her occupied without screen time.

If there’s one small quibble, the glue pages are best used with a regular glue stick rather than the included paste to avoid mess, but that’s a minor issue and expected with kids’ activity books. Overall, a great purchase — affordable, high-quality, and thoughtfully designed for young children. I’d definitely buy other titles in this series and recommend it to parents looking for an engaging, educational sticker activity book.

title: Unoriginal and Uninspiring
text: If you happened upon this book by chance and are looking for some quantitative market insights, then do not be fooled by the books title. From a knowledge perspective the book is worthless. There are plenty of better books on investment theory. Paulos has "regressed to the mean" here. This work merely capitalises on his previous, better efforts. The book is tedious, and in many respects his arguments are fallacious. For example he postulates that if most investors became indexers then markets would cease to be efficient. This is not supported by economic theory, where the contrary holds. It only takes a small number of active investors to retain market efficiency. If you are in search of investment knowledge you will be well served by the author Ron Ross in "Unbeatable Markets". Paulos has not made a contribution here, he has merely compiled a collection of anecdotes from other authors and tried to spin it to make it look like his own. His humour didn't work for me either. If you insist you have to buy the book based on the balance of reader reviews let it be known that you have been warned.

title: Not for everyone, but provides unique principles to filter through the "noise"
text:
In today's work ecosystem of forced multitasking, being "busy" all the time, and never feeling comfortable saying "no", Essentialism provides unique principles for sorting through the noise and figuring out what is truly "essential". The author himself says brilliantly that "essentialism is not one more thing -- it's a whole new way of doing everything". The key principles that I have uncovered from this book are the following:
(1) Work effectively, not efficiently (the latter does not imply that you are working on THE most important things)
(2) Learn to say no to things (personal, work, etc) and take greater control of your life
(3) Actively funnel to-do's, requests, etc through an internal "essential" test to decide whether something is truely important and should be done at all

One caveat, similar to many books in this genre. If you are a low-ranking associate at your job, you will find it difficult to implement a fair number of these strategies Day 1 (e.g. "how the hell am I supposed to do this while working at a [law firm / bank / advertising agency / etc]). That being said, the principles are still worth reading and keeping with you, because as you grow more senior in your role (even if you're just managing one person initially), they will become incrementally more valuable

title: A Concise & Well-Written Treatise on Freedom.
text:
This thin book is packed with common sense about politics and freedom. And although I knew most of the positions Ron Paul supports and the evidence for them, I still learned some new things.

My favorite quote from the entire book: "Truth is treason in the empire of lies." Oh man, that's a zinger. And it describes our current political environment perfectly.

My only criticism of the book is minor: He brings up the issue of 9/11 briefly, but speaks as if terrorists were solely responsible for it. I suppose the book would've gotten way off track if he had mentioned it, but there's plenty of evidence that 9/11 was an inside job. And I'm not only referring to "Loose Change." (Take Robin Hordon's testimony, for instance, among many others.)

If we don't make changes, we're bound for tough times ahead. This quote from the book sums up well where we're headed:

"Any government that inflates the money supply runs the risk of hyperinflation, which occurs when the money supply is increased so much as to render the currency completely worthless. [...] The textbook case in the twentieth century took place in Germany in 1923. [...] The result was the complete ruin of the German mark, which German children began gluing together to make kites and German adults burned in order to keep warm." (p. 150-151)

title: Love
text:
I bought Love on a whim after seeing it recommended during a rough week, and I’m honestly amazed at how much it’s become a small daily ritual in our household. The box arrived quickly and intact, and right away I appreciated the quality — sturdy components and thoughtful design that don’t feel cheap or gimmicky.

This isn’t a traditional toy; it’s a game/experience that prompts real connection. The prompts are varied and well-written: some are light and playful, others nudge you toward deeper conversations. My partner and I have used it both during quiet evenings and on road trips, and each time it opens up topics we might not have touched otherwise. We’ve had laughs, surprised moments, and a few genuinely meaningful talks. It’s helped us remember things we love about each other and discover new things too.

I also gifted it to friends who recently got engaged, and they reported back that it became a favorite date-night activity. The format is flexible — you can play seriously, skip prompts you’re not comfortable with, or use it as a jumping-off point for longer discussions. The cards (or components) are clearly organized, and the instructions are simple.

My only minor critique: I’d like a few more cards geared toward lighter, goofy prompts — there’s a slight bias toward introspection, which is great most of the time but sometimes feels heavy after a long day. Otherwise, this product delivers what it promises: a way to foster closeness and communication without feeling forced.

If you want a thoughtful, easy-to-use tool to deepen relationships — romantic or otherwise — this is worth adding to your shelf. We use it regularly and always come away feeling more connected.

title: More informative than grouchy!
text:
"The Grouchy Grammarian" is not a grouchy book. Parrish's fictional curmudgeon limits his irritation to public figures and national media outlets for spreading grammatical errors and "infelicities" throughout the populace. Parrish constructively channels his alter-ego's concerns, and the result is enlightening rather than chastening. Among usage guides, this one is particularly helpful for three reasons:
1) Each topic is covered in a short chapter, and each chapter ends with a summary so you can learn a lot quickly.
2) Parrish includes a thorough index, and a thoughtful annotated bibliography of guides to language, writing and usage.
3) Parrish clearly explains why usage glitches are glitches. Now that I understand what NOT to do, I don't have to laboriously memorize rules about what to do. Rote memorization of grammar rules never worked for me--I resemble the student in "Up the Down Staircase" who complains that "semicolons don't stick to my head."
I wish all people who worry about "weak", "watery" assaults upon English had mediators like Parrish to absorb their ire and deftly convey their championship and knowledge of precise language.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to sit down and share how profoundly it changed my understanding of politics. From the first chapter I felt like someone had taken the noise out of the room and handed me a clear map. The author explains complex ideas with patience and real-world examples, making abstract theories feel relevant to everyday decisions and debates.

What I appreciated most was the balance: this is not polemic or partisan sloganeering. Instead, it's an invitation to think critically about institutions, incentives, and the incentives of the people who operate within them. The historical context and case studies are carefully chosen and well-researched, yet rendered in an approachable style that never talks down to the reader. I learned new frameworks for evaluating policy proposals and interpreting political behavior, and those frameworks have already changed how I read the news and discuss politics with friends.

The book is also practical — it offers tools for civic engagement that are realistic rather than utopian, which I found refreshingly honest. If you care about understanding why political systems behave as they do and want to be better informed (not just louder), this is one of the most enlightening books on the subject I've read. Highly recommended.

title: Decent product, good price, functions as advertised
text:
tl;dr version: For $32 you can't go wrong.

I've been using this backpack cooler almost daily since I bought it two weeks ago. I use three, small rectangular "blue ice" packs placed on the bottom, on top of a small, folded dish towel to absorb any condensation. I haven't used it with ice. Some reviewers say the top zipper leaks if you use ice that melts. I can well imagine...so don't use ice.

There is plenty of room in this thing for enough food and drinks for two or three people. It's kept me fed through a few double shifts and everything stays cold for a good 20 hours. The blue ice packs are still half-frozen after that long. I live in a temperate part of the country, I can't say anyone in Arizona or Nevada, for instance, would have the same results, so caveat emptor.

The straps are long and wide enough to be comfortable when wearing this as a backpack, and I'm a pretty big guy. It also carries well slung over one shoulder, which is not always the case.

Some of the reviews fault the zippers for breaking. Yeah, I can see that happening if you jerk them, are impatient, or in a hurry and not paying attention. I've had no problems with them. Same with the stitching; I pack out at about 20 pounds and I've seen no signs of wear and tear, yet. It has only been two weeks, sure, but still...

Pros: keeps food plenty cold for a whole day when used with re-freezable ice packs; lots of room inside, comfortable straps. Netting pockets for water bottles, etc. on the sides are deep and big enough for wide bottles.

Cons: zippered storage compartments on the front and top are inadequate. No "waterproof" storage compartment for keys, phone, etc.

I’ve been using this product for a few weeks now and overall I’m pleased with the results. The packaging was simple but sturdy, and it arrived quickly with no damage. The texture is pleasant—lightweight and not sticky—and it applies smoothly, absorbing into my skin without leaving a greasy residue. I’ve noticed my skin looks a bit brighter and feels softer after regular use, though it didn’t completely erase my problem areas (fine lines and occasional dryness). For the price, I think it offers good value.

A couple of minor drawbacks: the scent is mildly floral and not overpowering, but if you’re sensitive to fragrance you might prefer something fragrance-free. Also the pump can be a little fussy at first, requiring a couple of presses to get product out. Customer service answered my question promptly when I reached out, which was a plus. I’d buy this again and would recommend it to someone looking for a reliable, reasonably priced addition to their skincare routine.

The only problem (minor) that I had with this table is there are some small scratches or gouges in the wood. Some of it is on the underside of the table so you cannot see it, but some is visible. For the $36 I paid for this table, I can deal with some small cosmetic damage. I actually ordered three total of these tables. Overall I give this 4 stars, 4.5 if they had it. The only reason this table did not get 5 stars is because of the minor cosmetic stuff. This is a great table, one that I would recommend to those who don't want to spend a fortune and can deal with some small scratches.

In An Unlikely Suitor, Ms. Moser takes the reader back to another time and place. While she expertly creates a picture of the poor of New York City in the late 1800s, she also recreates the magic of Newport, RI during the same time. The beginnings of three couples were beautifully woven together seamlessly. The author brought both the society of the time and the fashions of the time to life!

In practice it’s a mixed bag, and I’m giving it two stars because of one major issue that ruins most of the experience: it is the squeakiest chair I have ever owned.

Right out of the box the frame seemed solid and the fabric felt ok for the price. Setup was straightforward and the chair folded down to a nice compact carry size. It is reasonably light and the included carry bag is handy, which is why I still use it occasionally despite the problem.

But when you sit down and shift even slightly, the metal frame lets out a loud, high-pitched squeak. Moving from standing to seated is like a chorus of tiny brakes. At a quiet campsite or during a game, the noise is embarrassing and constant. I tried tightening all the screws, applying lubricant to the joints, and even layering some cloth at the contact points — nothing fully fixed it. The squeak is present whether the chair is placed on grass, gravel, or concrete.

Comfort-wise, the seat is average for a folding chair. The back offers minimal support and after a couple hours you start to feel it. The cup holder is useful but flimsy. Weight capacity seems fine for my needs, and the fabric has held up after a few uses.

If you only need an inexpensive portable chair and can tolerate (or fix) the noise, it serves a purpose. But if you want quiet, comfortable seating for longer outdoor events, look elsewhere. I’m disappointed because the price and portability were appealing, but the constant squeaking makes it more trouble than it’s worth.

text: We have a large-breed dog (Akita) Rescue and wash lots of dog bowls. We first fell in love with Scrub Daddy because you can use it over and over again with no mildew smell. At first, we were willing to forgive the high price for the little happy face on "daddy" but rather quickly, too quickly, in fact, his face went from happy to sad. In fact, he was downright distraught while sitting on the counter and he flopped around in our hand making it difficult to use. We then stumbled on the Lunatec. Yes, it's a little different. Like a dish cloth but ...more...nylon-netty and flimsy. But that's what makes it perfect! The Luncatec can lay across a finger tip and wipe inside a water bottle or other small area, lay flat and wash out a large water trough or bowl, or, fold it in half or quarters for a scrub-pad effect. A Scrub Buddy, with average use (used twice a day on 6 bowls) lasted about 2 weeks. So far, the Lunatec has been here and after nearly 3 weeks, shows ZERO signs of wear. No smell, no scudge, no bacteria. Just clean, clean, scrubbing and clean clean bowls. Oh, we noted another reviewer was unhappy with the Lunatec because he said he washed out a bowl with bread dough and it clogged the Lunatec. Well, duh, or, should we say "Doh!" You should expect that result with ANY type of sponge or cloth and a gooey/gummy dough. When we make bread or macaroni and cheese and have gooey bowls, we use plastic pan scrapers or a hard sink brush to knock off all the gooey/gummy stuff first and then use a sponge or cloth to do the washing/sanitizing. One Scrub Daddy for $8.50 or FOUR (4) Lunatec's for $7.50. The choice is simple, we think. This product stands up, does MORE than it should, and for that, we love you, you Lunatec!

First of all, this puzzle, which is the size of two old 45 records stacked atop one another, arrives in a plastic package the size of your house.

Nor is this like a Rubik’s Cube, where after you solve it, it’s fun to mix it up and try again. I haven’t had the urge to pick it up again after my initial tests, which I think says something.

Bottom line: extremely wasteful packaging containing a no-challenge “puzzle.” Maybe this would be better marketed as a fidget toy. Or to very small children. Would not recommend.

text:
I had recently read this book because of a Creative Writing assignment. The reason I chose this book is because reading it took me way back to when my mind was early in the stage of the exploration of literature. I owned this book as a child, and reading it gave me another small perspective on how our own life and time itself progresses.

Robert Munsch uses humour in alot of his books and this is another one of those cases. For example, at the end of this book, the child's father is suspended in the middle of the kitchen by his toe with a long rope.

Munsch also uses a form of anticipation to ensure that the child >wants< to turn to the next page. For example, most of the pages in this book have sentences that end like: "He looked in the kitchen, it was empty. He looked in the bathroom, it was empty. He looked in the garage and..."

title: Excellent Zoom, Great Pics
text:
This camera replaced my previous Canon (3MP PowerShot S30). I will only buy Canon cameras, their picture quality is superb for a point-n-shoot. What sold me on the SX120IS was the 10X optical zoom.

The 10X optical zoom is spectacular! It gets wonderful pictures of our kids on the baseball field, and at concerts and shows. Pictures that 3X optical zoom could never do. Pictures from 100 ft look like you were standing only 15 ft away. I've had other parents ask me to take pictures of their kids, because they couldn't get close enough for a good shot. Yes, 10X is awesome.

The 10 megapixels are good, and the pictures are still great, but I am not impressed by pixel count. The overall picture quality is as good as my previous 3 MP canon, but not better. However, now the files are 3.3 times larger on my hard drive. Slower to open, slower to upload to web, and harder to email. The up-side to 10 MP is when pictures need cropped, there are still plenty of pixels remaining to make a good 8.5x11 print.

Do not be taken by the 3.0" LCD. Yes, it is big. But the resolution is not tight, so even though the LCD is bigger there aren't more pixels in it. And the menu fonts are big. I would have been just as happy with a 2.5" LCD with a tighter resolution.

All of the shooting modes are great, and easy to use. This camera has more "special" modes than my last camera, and they are nice. But one mode it does not have, and I miss it, is the panoramic stitch-assist mode. If you try to do a pano stitch with this camera, you'll have to guess at where you left off.

Overall this is a great camera. I would recommend it to anyone who wants beautiful pictures and a lot of optical zoom. Can't beat the price either.
