text: Melanie Rawn is an outstanding writer who intuitively captures the soul of each of her characters and the flavor of their personalities as formed and flawed by experiences within the various shirs, especially the starkness of  The Waste, in which they live and love. She provides colorful and rich  variations on power lust and delicious sexuality that tantalize and reveal.  Exiles and Mageborn Traitor,present a matriarchial society of women as  power brokers and males the home/care givers that challenges the reader to  think about how this could be in "real" life. Her characters are  drawn with insight and thoughtfulness kissed with great wit and wry humor.  She informs the reader of alternate points of view with the graceful  brushstroke of gentle humanity in a smooth, refreshing and thought  provoking way, even when the characters are the villians!  Here is great  mastery in her enchanting style of wrapping you within the cocoon of her  stories where you connect with her characters and what they find funny. The  brilliant description of the arrogant, self absorbed, corpulent,"Grand  Duchess" of Domburr over dressed in gauche yellow riding clothes, with  an orange scarf tied under her chins, heaving her massive bulk onto an even  more massive "plow horse" to go on a hunt is just hilarious. This  dazzling humor is prevalent in her Dragon Prince and Dragon Token series  (which are forerunners in style to this series).  Here we find an even more  powerful fantasy slice of life for those of us addicted to Ms. Rawn's  excellence in writing as her wittiness and sly humor weaves its magical  thread throughout which makes her work so welcome to read.  I look forward  to the blow out mage war between the meleressi and mage guardians in the  forthcoming book Captal's Tower. You can bet Jored and Josselyn will be  nose to toes in that battle!  Will Cailet finds her true love? (Josselyn? )  Will Sarra find someone to ease her broken heart, share her political  battles and warm her lusty nights? Will Teigan's wrenching struggle to open  up to her magic persist after  Glenin's murder of her beloved father?  Will her twin Mikel's magic be supplanted by his evolution into  minstel/bard in Collan/Falundir's place? text:
I've used Gatorskins for years, riding my Specialized Tarmac SL2 in the hills surrounding the San Francisco Bay Area. The shoulders of these near-urban backroads tend to be strewn with debris and there's plenty of shattered glass remnants from long-ago broken bottles. (No street sweepers set foot on these roads!)

Even though I've got a fancy lightweight racebike, I put up with the added rolling weight of Conti's Gatorskins because when I used to ride with "racing" clinchers, I'd get two or three flats a month. And I hate fixing flats! Spoils the rhythm of my ride!

My last set of Gatorskins lasted two seasons. This time, when ordering replacements, I opted for the "Hardshell" version. And let me tell you, there's a difference in the riding experience. The hardshell component is a thick layer of solid rubber over the middle of the tire. When inflated at the recommended pressure (110 psi), I'm feeling every bump and pebble I ride over quite a bit more than was my experience with regular Gatorskins. My sense is that the thick rubber in the center is reducing the bump-absorbing effects that make pneumatic tires essential on most vehicles.

No doubt as these Hardshells tires wear, the ride will become less stiff. And I wouldn't be surprised if all that extra rubber gave me an extra season's life from my set of tires. But I've got to say, I miss the shock absorbtion of my regular Gatorskins. When the time comes to replace these Hardshells, I'll probably go back to the non-Hardshell Gators. They gave me all the flat protection I needed and provided a comfy ride as well.

title: Reliable printer and a good value
text:
I’ve been using this printer in my home office for about three months now and overall I’m very pleased with its reliability and value. Before buying I was primarily looking for something that would handle a moderate amount of printing — invoices, shipping labels, a few flyers, and the occasional photo — without fuss or a lot of maintenance. This model has mostly delivered on that promise.

Setup was straightforward. The software package included everything I needed and the wireless setup with my laptop and phone was quick and stable. I liked that the control panel is simple; no confusing menus or tiny icons. It connects to my network without dropping out, which was a major plus compared to a previous model I owned.

Print quality is good for everyday documents. Text comes out crisp and dark, and the pages are well-aligned. Color prints are decent for internal use—presentations and handouts look professional enough—but if you want gallery-quality photos, a dedicated photo printer would still be the better choice. Print speed is reasonable for a home office; large jobs take some time but nothing excessive. I appreciate that the printer doesn’t make a lot of noise during operation.

One of the strongest points is reliability. I’ve had very few paper jams and the ones that did occur were easy to clear thanks to accessible panels. Ink usage seems efficient; I get a fair number of pages per cartridge. Replacement cartridges aren’t the cheapest on the market, but they are competitively priced and easy to find, which reinforces the overall value proposition.

There are a couple of minor drawbacks. The mobile app is functional but lacks a few advanced features I’ve seen with other brands, and occasionally the scanner takes a second try to capture documents perfectly aligned. Also, while the machine supports automatic duplex printing, it sometimes hesitates on thicker paper types.

For the price point, this printer hits most marks: dependable, easy to use, and cost-effective for regular office tasks. I’m giving it four stars rather than five because of the few small quirks and because it’s not the absolute best choice if your primary need is high-end photo printing. If you need a solid, no-nonsense printer for everyday office work, this is a very good option.

text:
Chariton explores a number of questions revolving around the tragedy of Alamo. Most of the questions he explores are, in fact, not legends but legitimate questions as to what did or did not happen in an around the time that the Alamo was attacked and the defenders slaughtered. Generally I agree with Chariton's deductions although I also believe that all testimony regarding the Zuber must regarded with extreme suspicion. Zuber claimed that he got his information from Louis Rose, the supposed only deserter from Alamo. In a manner resembling Thucidides, Zuber admitted embellishing [making up] Travis' final speech to the troops, including the famous 'line in the sand'. In my opinion, if Zuber lied about anything, then it should be rightfully assumed that he lied about everything.

I think Zuber's testimony is an insult to all the men who died at Alamo. Their heroism stands by itself and required no second hand editorialism. I'll go even further than that to proclaim my own belief that Louis Rose--if he ever existed--never testified to Zuber. Zuber made up the entire story 'whole-cloth'.

Ron

title: The Irish Banana Review
text:
Ask the Passengers is exactly the type of book you think you're getting when you read the summary: It's a book about a teenage girl who is trying to sort out her life and figure out who she is and who she wants to be. And yes, it has the added twist of the main character coming to terms with her sexual orientation.

I was a little surprised at how ordinary Astrid felt. Not that I expected her to be some dramatic, overblown character, but I felt like there was nothing spectacular that set her apart from a lot of the other teenage girls I read about in contemporary novels. Her parents don't get her--her mom is more concerned with her sister and her dad is fairly oblivious. That just felt formulaic to me. Aside from the lesbian angle to the story, Astrid felt like any other girl dealing with feelings for that special someone, but unsure of how to express them.

This book is all about emotion. I expected that going in, and A.S. King really does a nice job of expressing those emotions. She phrases things splendidly, and I truly enjoy her writing style. The story flowed nicely. It wasn't overly long or excessively wordy, which could have been an easy pitfall to stumble into.

Overall, this book was exactly what I expected, but that's what disappointed me. I was hoping for something that would wow me. Something I could get really excited about and sink into. The setting is a small town where everyone knows everyone's business, but again, that just felt so done already. I feel like I've read variations of this novel before, but the way King wrote it kept me engaged to the end.

text:
I bought the Up as a gift for my teenage son who’s been getting into trail running and cycling, and it’s become one of those rare purchases that actually exceeds expectations. Right out of the box the unit felt solid and well-made. Setup was straightforward — the quick-start guide was clear, and pairing with my phone took two minutes. The app is intuitive and gives useful summaries without being cluttered.

The first thing that struck me was the accuracy of the activity tracking. Steps, distance, and elevation on hikes matched the readouts on his watch and my bike computer within a small margin. Sleep tracking has been surprisingly helpful: he used to complain about feeling tired all day, but after a few nights of reviewing the detailed sleep stages and suggestions, he changed his evening routine and now reports waking up more refreshed. Battery life is strong; we go several days between charges even with nightly sleep monitoring enabled.

For someone active, the Up’s fitness coaching features are a standout. The guided goals and gentle reminders helped him increase daily movement without feeling nagged. It also integrates nicely with other apps we use for running, so we didn’t have to manually transfer data. Durability has been impressive — it’s been knocked, splashed, and worn during muddy trail runs and still looks and functions like new.

A few relatively minor quibbles: the band could be a touch softer for all-day comfort, especially in hot weather, and the vibration alerts are on the light side (easy to miss during a loud workout). Also, the app’s social/competitions features are a bit basic compared to larger ecosystems, but that’s not a dealbreaker for us.

Overall, the Up hits the sweet spot for reliable tracking, helpful coaching, and good battery life in a rugged package. My son is using it daily and his activity levels have gone up noticeably. If you want a solid, no-fuss tracker that actually helps you move more and sleep better, this one is well worth the price.

text:
How many creative ways can one pose the vulgar? And we don't mean pose in the effete way, either. Perhaps this book will make you feel like Charles Manson playing the kazoo before an audience of irritable emperor penguins. Maybe.

It is hard not to take the printed "volume one" as anything but a threat, but it is a kindly one under the care of a good reader. Spitzer's short rocket-style blasts of the absurd, visceral, and tradition-baiting vulgarity makes for that kind of nostalgic reading many of us had as kids with the flashlight under the bed covers reading Mad Magazine. If you liked Spitzer's "Riding the Unit", you'll most definitely enjoy this more. In some ways, the irreal-ist quality of these shorts, wondrously masked by trademark obscenity, turns The Art of Fiction (1984) on its ear. Again, maybe.

There's simply not one bit of bathos in the whole lot, so hang on tight to your lawn furniture and have this book kicking around your cottage this summer.

The themes felt timely without being preachy. Issues around identity, belonging, and forgiveness are woven into the narrative in a way that made me reflect on my own life long after I finished. The setting is vividly drawn; I could picture scenes clearly, and certain passages transported me to specific seasons and smells in a way that great novels do.

Formatting and editing were clean—no distracting typos—so my reading flow was uninterrupted. I'm recommending this to friends who like literary fiction with heart and readers who enjoy emotionally intelligent storytelling. text:
I was delighted to find this author, known for his travel narratives and splendid prose, an Englishman born in 1908 and only dying recently at age 95 in Saffron Walden, Essex, where he had lived modestly and politely, shyly even. Luigi Barzini described reading his prose as "like eating cherries" and Graham Greene - with whom Lewis shared many similarities in adventures, courage and quiet, commanding prose - had "no hesitation in calling him one of the best writers, not of any particular decade, but of our century".

In this work - part of a multiple volume autobiography, there was only one decision Lewis made that damaged his intellect in this readers view - he agreed to an investigative reporting trip to Peru accompanied by Lord Snowden as his photographer, traveling "incognito". Lewis seemed genuinely surprised that was far from a successful trip, or experience, and as for the `incognito' - well at least it got the author free upgrades to First Class flights and entertainment by British Ambassadors and Peruvian society!

The author had a fascinating and often wildly exciting life, serving in the British Forces in Italy during WWII followed by a career in journalism reporting on Vietnam, Burma, Indo China and producing a splendid series of books for Jonathan Cape - who used to entertain his authors with dinners of burnt Irish Stew - on the mafia in Sicily, and the threatened indigenous peoples of Latin America.

Writing with a compassion and light wit Lewis crafted over thirty books and one of his five children, his second son Gareth, has also published a book called 'Deceit'.

title: Will not fit regular kayak paddles
text:
I bought this paddle holder hoping it would keep my regular kayak paddles secure on the roof while transporting my boat. The idea and construction seemed solid in the photos, and I liked the price, so I gave it a try. After a few uses I have mixed feelings — mostly frustration.

First, the good: the materials feel reasonably sturdy for the price. The straps are thick and have robust buckles, and the foam cradle is dense enough that it didn’t collapse under the weight of the paddle. Installation on my roof rack was straightforward, and it didn’t shift around while driving once tightened. For small, slim paddles or very compact touring blades, I think this could work fine.

Now the big problem: it won’t fit standard kayak paddles. I have two common-size paddles (Suvine touring paddles, about 2.25" shaft diameter with modestly sized blades) and they simply don’t sit in the cradle the way the photos imply. The opening is too narrow and the foam forms around the shaft so tightly that you can’t get the paddles into position without bending them, which of course you should not do. I tried rotating and angling them, but they either won’t sit centered or the blades interfere with the straps. The product would work much better if the cradle opening were wider or if additional foam spacers were removable to accept larger shafts.

Customer support was polite when I contacted them, but their suggestion was to “force” the paddle in or swap to a different paddle size, which isn’t acceptable. For anyone with standard kayak paddles, I can’t recommend this unless you plan to modify it yourself (cutting foam out or replacing the cradle). Considering the decent build but critical sizing issue, two stars feels fair — it has potential but fails at the main purpose I bought it for.

Only minor drawback is that it’s a bit pricier than some drugstore options, but given the effectiveness and how little product I need per use, it’s worth the cost for me. If you have dry or sensitive skin and are tired of temporary fixes, give this a try—you might be as pleased with it as I am. Five stars.

title: Mixed Emotions
text:
A dark and foreboding novel of a thousands years ago -- the coldness of the climate and the land accentuated by the lack of the sun's light -- although it teasingly seems to appear on the horizon to prematurely announce its impending return.

"The Wolf in the Whale" is populated by ancient, mysterious, powerful and hardy people - Norsemen and women living, fighting and dying in a new world. The whole novel brings with it a sense of perpetual cold and darkness.

The spirits seem to reign in this book -- they talk to the shamans young and old, and bestow upon them certain powers as the situations deem -- The chief protagonists are a young girl and her older brother, who use their wits to survive -- and who are transmuted back and forth to animal spirits and back again to human.

The narrative is excellent - one can feel the harsh living conditions and can be caught up in the spirit world that revolves around each person like a whirlpool of snow and cold air. The veil between the spirit, animal and human world is very thin indeed.

However, I felt that the book dragged on for too long -- and after a while this reader began to feel mired down in spots, as if walking thru a powdery snow capped with thin ice - very slow going.

So although "The Wolf in the Whale" transported me quite well, back to an era where the spirits and animals spoke with and transferred powers on primitive warrior humans fighting to survive in a cold and forbidding land - it was a wearying journey for me, as it was, IMHO, far too long.

title: Well made hat to protect against sunburn
text:
I bought this sun hat before a week-long beach trip and it has become my go-to item whenever I’m planning to be outside for more than an hour. Right out of the box you can tell it’s well made — the stitching is even, the brim keeps its shape, and the fabric feels substantial without being heavy. I needed something that would actually protect my face and neck from prolonged sun exposure, and this hat exceeded my expectations.

The brim is wide enough to shade my entire face and most of my neck when I’m standing or sitting, and it doesn’t flop down into my eyes like some floppy hats do. It has a slight wire or reinforcement around the edge that holds the shape but still allows me to fold it for packing. I was able to flatten it into my beach bag for travel and it popped back into shape perfectly when I took it out.

Comfort is another big plus. The inner band is soft and didn’t irritate my forehead even after hours of wear. There’s an adjustable chin cord that keeps the hat secure when it’s windy — I was grateful for that on a blustery coastline day. I also appreciated the ventilation panels (or breathable weave) that kept my head from getting too hot; I didn’t sweat nearly as much as I expected, even in direct sun and humidity.

Functionally it delivers on sun protection: paired with sunscreen I avoided any sunburn on my face and ears the entire trip. The color held up too — I picked a light neutral that didn’t fade after multiple outings. It’s easy to clean; a quick hand wash and air dry got rid of salt and sunscreen residue.

If I have any minor nitpicks, it’s that the sizing runs a touch large on my small head even tightened to the smallest setting, but the chin cord always keeps it snug. Also, it’s not a fashion statement — it’s clearly built for function over runway style — but I don’t mind that at all for what I bought it for.

Overall, great quality, very practical, and built to last. If you’re looking for a reliable hat to protect against sunburn during outdoor activities, this is a solid choice.

title: Afghanistan through the eyes of a child
text: A war-torn country plagued by violence.  An 11-year-old girl forced to risk her life and save her family. These are the realities in Deborah Ellis' novel "The Breadwinner" (Groundwood Books 2000).  Told from young Parvana's perspective, the story focuses on her family of six living in Kabul, Afghanistan.  After the Taliban take control of their city, Parvana's family is forced out of their large home by a bomb explosion and into a one-room apartment.  The women are removed from school and forced to stay in the house unless escorted by a male.  When Parvana's father is arrested because he attended university in England, their family must make the tough decision to have her pose as a boy in order to leave the house and work in the marketplace to earn money for food.  While working, Parvana runs into Shauzia, a girl she knew from school who is also posing as a boy to support her family. They start to work together and soon become close friends, encountering a number of sobering, scary situations along the way. Though children may not experience the same life, they will no doubt relate to Parvana's story and her arguments with her older sister, unfairness of chore responsibilities, and love for her family.  The Breadwinner is not a happy story with a happy conclusion, but one that will leave the reader with a different view of Afghanistan, as seen through the eyes of a child.  An author's note and glossary of terms serve as a helpful aide in introducing children to the history and culture of Afghanistan.

Another small but important detail: the mitt prevents staining on my palms and nails. It has a nice inner lining that keeps my hands clean and comfortable throughout application. I’ve recommended this mitt to friends and family who’ve noticed a real difference in their self-tanning results.

If you self-tan regularly or are looking to upgrade from disposable gloves, this mitt is worth every penny. It makes applying self-tanner fast, neat, and foolproof. Five stars.

title: Limited, superficial, and incomplete (for those who know0
text:
For those who don't know the depth and breadth of Qigong as field of endeavor (not a singular art) with very diverse practices, this is a taste-tester's manual on the topic concerning one of the oldest Qigong systems on record. The problem is ...

(1) it only covers two of the five animals from the ancient sage physician Hua Tou. Which means one's practice is incomplete and out of balance for this particular system.

(2) that no modern scholars are truly certain of how these exercises were conducted, since we have only the sage physician's written descriptions (and not extensive ones) mixed with some cave drawings, and

(3) there are better works that attempt to address not only their own speculations on how these exercises were conducted but also attempt to support such with scholarship and reasoning, drawing on comparative arts inside and outside of the Qigong field, and stepping well beyond mere two sentence sketchy definitions of romanized Chinese terms... as is the case in this book.

If you would like a simple and short manual with direct instructions for soft exercises that might not do enough for you, then maybe this is for you. Or if you're another new ager looking for your next step on a path likely leading nowhere, then this is for you. If you want to explore the range of speculations on this ancient Qigong system, then you might also consider buying it... but only after you've acquired other more comprehensive works on the topic.

title: Very good performance at a nice prices.
text:
The scale was relatively cheap so I was concerned about its precision and accuracy, so I weight 6 coins to see if the claims could be verified. The test showed the Standard Deviation of the measurements was less that one milligram per gram. As to the accuracy the standard provided was not much use as it was probably used to do the initial calibration of the scale, but it was useful in assessing the repeatability, which was very good. I got 100 grams each time I weighted it. To get an idea about the accuracy I used the coins, which when new have very consistent weights. The coin test showed about 0.25% deviation from what clean new coins should have weighed. As the coins were neither new or clean, in my opinion, this is very good for a scale of this price. As I am going to use the scale to titrate my medicines, the accuracy and repeatability are very important to me. These scales appear to be way within my criteria. The scale appears to be well made, but at this time I have no idea how reliable it is.

Now the bad news: parts of the protective shielding were not included in the package. The vendor promised to send me the missing parts but they have not arrived yet. I’ll update this review in two weeks or so with an assessment of the vendors performance. Update: they arrived!

I have found the scale is repeatable, but is does not respond to a small load change. Say 4 mg plus or minus. The work around is to put pressure on the scale for a second or so and it will adjust the reading correctly. This second delay is a little irritating but it probably deals with air currents and vibrations constantly changing the readings and the microprocessor spending time averaging the readings. I have been titrating one of my meds to 1.375 mg dose, which works out to 60 mg of the ground up tablets and I was able keep 37 doses all with in +/- 1.5%

title: Good to have on hand for emergencies

The carrying case is tough and zips securely so nothing shifts around, and it fits easily under the seat.

What I appreciate most is the selection of items. There are basics you actually need in a roadside situation: a bright emergency blanket, a sturdy reflective vest, heavy-duty gloves, a dependable flashlight with extra batteries, and a first-aid kit that contains more than just a few adhesive bandages. The jumper cables are solid and come in a pouch to keep them from tangling. There’s also a multi-tool and a seatbelt cutter/window breaker — small additions that give real peace of mind.

Quality feels good for the price. Nothing in the kit feels cheap or likely to fail when you need it. The reflective strips and vest are visible from a distance, and the flashlight is brighter than I expected. The first-aid supplies are clearly labeled and the manual included is straightforward and useful for non-medical people like me.

I’ve used a couple of items already — the blanket and gloves — and they stood up to use without issue. Even if you never need to use most of it, having this kit in your car reduces stress when things go wrong. For weekend camping or keeping in a sports bag, it’s just as handy. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a well-rounded, reliable emergency kit without overpaying.

text:
I bought this chair because the listing promised “plush seating” and “all-day comfort,” but what arrived could not be further from that description. The seat is not cushiony at all — it’s hard and flat, with a thin foam layer that compresses immediately and leaves you feeling like you’re sitting on a board. After just 20–30 minutes I started shifting constantly trying to find a comfortable position. I’ve tried adding a seat pad and a small pillow, which helped marginally, but it defeats the purpose of buying a supposedly comfortable chair.

The upholstery feels cheap and slightly rough to the touch, not the soft fabric that the pictures suggested. The seams around the cushion area are already showing signs of stress where my weight concentrates, and I’m worried about long-term durability. Assembly was OK if you’re handy, but the parts didn’t feel sturdy and the frame creaked a little the first week I used it.

What bothered me most was the misleading product copy and photos. If the manufacturer had called this a minimalist dining chair with thin padding, I would have understood the lower cost. But advertising it as “plush” and “supportive” set expectations that were never met. For short visits it’s tolerable, but for working from home, long meals, or reading, it’s uncomfortable.

I’m returning it and looking for a chair with actual cushioning and better build quality. Save yourself the hassle and avoid this if comfort is important to you.

title: Very easy to fly
text:
I bought this drone for my 12-year-old after reading that it was “very easy to fly,” and overall it has delivered on that promise. Right out of the box the setup was straightforward — charged the battery, synced the controller, and we were hovering in the backyard within ten minutes. The controls are responsive and intuitive; the beginner mode is especially helpful for someone just learning how to keep a steady hover and make gentle turns.

The flight stability is impressive for a toy in this price range. Even on slightly windy days it holds position well, and the built-in altitude hold keeps it from drifting up or down unexpectedly. The battery life is okay — we get about 8–10 minutes per charge, which is typical for toys at this level. I purchased an extra battery and that doubled our playtime without much fuss.

Camera is decent for casual footage; not high-res but fine for family videos and a few fun clips to share. The drone is fairly durable too — it survived a couple of hard landings without damage to the propellers or body, which gave me confidence that it will last through normal kid use.

Why four stars and not five? Two small complaints: the charging cable is short and the controller range could be a bit better for longer flights. Also, replacement parts aren’t super easy to find locally. Despite that, considering the price and how easy it is to learn, I’d recommend this as a great starter drone for kids and beginners.

title: Irritated
text:
I wanted to like this book — the premise sounded promising and the cover pulled me in — but overall I finished it feeling more irritated than satisfied. The pacing is uneven: long stretches of repetitive inner monologue interrupt what could have been tighter, more engaging scenes. Several plot threads are introduced but never properly resolved, which left me frustrated rather than intrigued.

The writing itself has moments of genuine insight, but they’re scattered between awkward phrasing and unnecessary tangents. I also felt the protagonist’s decisions were often contrived to force conflict rather than arising naturally from characterization. Secondary characters are thinly drawn, so it’s hard to invest emotionally in their outcomes.

On the positive side, the author clearly has a voice and some good ideas, and a few chapters genuinely resonated with me. But for the price, I expected a more polished and coherent read. I’d recommend this only to someone curious about the concept and willing to tolerate a messy execution.

title: Lois good on the counter
text:
I’ve been using the Lois “Good on the Counter” set for about six weeks and overall I’m pleased with the purchase — it’s earned a solid 4 stars from me. I bought it primarily as a functional and attractive way to keep small kitchen items tidy on my countertop, and it delivers on both counts.

The design is simple and modern, which fits nicely with my mostly neutral kitchen. The materials feel sturdy; the weighted base keeps it from tipping when I reach for items, and the finish has held up well to daily use and occasional splashes. Assembly was minimal and straightforward — just a few pieces that snapped together — and the whole unit feels well-made rather than cheap.

Functionally, it’s great for organizing cooking utensils, a couple of fresh fruit, and the stray mail and shopping list that always seems to collect on the counter. The compartments are a good size: deep enough for spatulas and wooden spoons, but not so wide that it dominates the counter. I also appreciate the little non-slip pads on the bottom that protect the surface beneath.

Why not five stars? A couple of small issues. First, the paint finish has started to show faint scuffs where metal utensils rub against it — not a dealbreaker, but noticeable if you look closely. Second, while the size is perfect for my apartment kitchen, it might be a bit small for someone who wants a true catch-all for larger items or a big family’s cooking tools. Finally, the price felt a touch high compared to similar organizers I’ve seen, though the build quality somewhat justifies it.

In short, the Lois counter organizer is a stylish, practical addition to a mid-sized kitchen. It looks good, functions well, and will keep your everyday items within reach — just temper expectations if you need heavy-duty capacity.

title: Sparks creativity, once you get past install problems
text:
The Digital Arts & Craft Studio from Fisher-Price is fun for the whole family (I think I used it more the first night than my 3 year old!), but you may be driven crazy by problems with the install process. Buyer beware if you are not willing to troubleshoot potential problems with buggy software.

In my case, I received the "Common Language Runtime Debugging error." If you do too, and your system meets the minimum requirements (and the firmware test, which comes with the software, works) then the problem is most likely your Microsoft .NET Framework installation.

I had 1.1 installed and it appears the program installs both a hotfix and .NET 2.0. To fix: uninstall everything (add/Remove programs). First, the Studio software, then NET 2.0, then the hotfix, and finally NET 1.1. Reboot, and reinstall from the CD. Everything should now work.

Took about an hour, but then we were up and running. Is it worth the money? My toddler is fascinated by the computer, and loves to draw, making this toy the perfect combination to keep her occupied (at least for a little while).

title: Chop Suey Culture
text:
If you like Chinese food, you should read this book. It will tell you everything you should have wondered about chop suey, fortune cookies, the Chinese restaurant industry and the Chinese people who have brought more than food to the United States

Ms. Lee uses her healthy curiosity and excellent research skills to study something we generally take for granted -- Chinese food is so unbiquitous as to be invisible, except when we're hungry. Being the daughter of Chinese immigrants and a New York Times reporter gives Ms. Lee the right lenses for studying her subject and produces insights that are subtle, interesting and thought-provoking. For example: How best to know the actual output of a Chinese restaurant when thinking about buying it? Count the garbage bags in the alley. Why were did Chinese laundries and restaurants survive 19th Century bigotry against the Chinese? Because cooking and washing were women's work and didn't threaten the white male labor force.

Equally as good as Ms. Lee's insights is her writing style. She has a tone that is a bit ironic, a bit whimsical. She appreciates the goofiness of what she is investigating, but also treats the topic respectfully. These are fine balances for a writer to maintain. And she brings many of her points home with a tidy turn of phrase: "Young professionals loved the idea that food could come from a phone rather than a stove." Or, "Common wisdom from one culture is perplexing in another." Or, finally, by describing American soy sauce as a "Frankensauce chemical counterfeit."

It powers on inconsistently; sometimes it boots, sometimes it needs multiple tries or unplugging to respond. When it does work, the advertised features are half-baked. The Bluetooth drops connection constantly, audio stutters, and pairing with my phone takes forever each time. The battery life is nowhere close to what the listing promised — I got maybe an hour and a half under light use, not the 6+ hours advertised.

Customer support was unhelpful. I contacted them about the defects and received generic troubleshooting steps that didn’t fix anything and no offer for a refund or replacement in a timely manner. text:

Overall I’m happy with the results — after about two weeks I noticed him getting up from the couch more easily and making longer walks without limping. The soft chews are easy to break in half for a smaller dose, and he takes them willingly with his food.

My only complaint is that the product has no smell at all. I was expecting at least a mild odor that would reassure me about the ingredients (especially since similar supplements often have a faint fish or liver scent). The neutral scent isn’t a dealbreaker, but it did make me double-check the packaging and batch number to make sure I’d received the right item. If you prefer odorless products, that could be a plus, but for me it felt slightly odd.

Packaging is sturdy and the seal held up during shipping. Price is reasonable compared to other brands, and the ingredient list is clean. I’ll likely reorder when this bottle runs out because the functional benefits for my dog are clear. Just know the product is essentially scentless.

title: Cat Scratching Post
text:
I bought this scratching post three months ago after my two indoor cats had almost shredded the armrests of my couch. I did a lot of searching for something sturdy, attractive enough to keep in the living room, and tall enough for them to fully stretch — this fit the bill perfectly.

Right out of the box assembly was quick and intuitive: two pieces snapped together and the base slides firmly into place. No tools required and the whole thing felt solid, not wobbly like some cheaper posts I’ve had. The surface is tightly wound sisal that resists fraying and seems to hold up well to daily use. Both of my cats prefer it over the old cardboard scratchers; I catch them using it multiple times a day, and the couch has been untouched for weeks.

The height is great for a full stretch and the diameter gives them a good grip without feeling flimsy. The base is weighted enough to prevent tipping, even when my bigger cat gives it an enthusiastic vertical clawing session. Cleaning is simple — vacuuming around the base removes loose fibers and occasional fur, and the material has not developed any unpleasant odor.

A couple of small points to note: one corner of the base upholstery started to peel slightly after heavy use, but it’s cosmetic and hasn’t affected functionality. Also, it’s not meant to be a cat tree replacement — there’s no platform to nap on — but that’s exactly what I wanted: a dedicated, effective scratching post.

Overall this is a well-made, effective scratching post that saved my furniture and that my cats clearly enjoy. I would buy it again and recommend it to any cat owner looking for a reliable, no-nonsense solution.

title: Great tent - try not to set it up alone.....
text:
I bought this tent for a weekend family camping trip and overall it exceeded my expectations — sturdy, roomy, and well thought out. We’re a family of four (two adults, two kids) and the tent comfortably fit two queen air mattresses plus gear along the perimeter with room to sit. The fabric feels durable and the seams look well sealed; after a night of heavy rain nothing leaked and the ground stayed dry. Ventilation is excellent — the mesh windows and ceiling kept the inside from getting stuffy even in the afternoon heat, and the guy lines and stakes held firm when the wind picked up.

My only serious caveat, and the reason for the title of this review, is setup. Instructions are adequate but the poles and clips require an extra set of hands. I tried to wrestle it up solo and made it more stressful and slower than necessary — there were a few moments where I wished for a partner to help hold corners while I threaded poles. With two people the setup took under 15 minutes. Takeaway: don’t plan to put it up alone if you want a quick, frustration-free start to your outing.

Small touches I appreciated: the vestibule for muddy boots, interior pockets for lights/phones, and the heavy-duty zippers that felt solid. The packed size is reasonable for car camping. If you need a reliable family tent and can have at least two people for setup, this is a great purchase. Highly recommend.

title: Love this game!
text:
I bought this game on a whim after seeing it recommended, and it has quickly become our go-to for family game nights. From the moment we opened the box, the components felt sturdy and well-made — the cards have a nice finish that resists wear, and the tokens are a good weight for little hands to handle. The rulebook is concise and easy to follow; we were playing within 15 minutes of unboxing.

What I appreciate most is the balance between strategy and luck. Younger players (my 8-year-old and 10-year-old) can grasp the basics right away and still feel like they have a real chance to win, while the adults enjoy the tactical choices that keep the game engaging round after round. Playtime is just right — long enough to feel satisfying, short enough to play multiple times in an evening or as a quick filler between other activities.

The replay value is excellent. There’s enough variety in the cards and scenarios that no two games feel identical, and the pacing keeps everyone involved. We’ve used it for casual family time, as a way to entertain visiting friends, and even for a low-pressure activity during a rainy afternoon. Cleanup is straightforward, and the box stores neatly on our shelf.

Minor quibble: a few components are a bit snug in the insert, but that’s a small trade-off for the overall quality. If you’re looking for a well-designed, fun game that’s accessible to a wide age range and delivers consistently entertaining sessions, I highly recommend this one. We’re already planning to bring it to our next game night.

title: The "gateway drone" for beginners
text:
I've never owned a drone before so didn't know what to expect. This package contains two zippable pouches with a folded controller and drone, which are both tiny. You have to charge both units before attempting anything, and the charging station isn't obvious to use. Next, install the app on your phone and it will sync with the drone later.

Once unfolded, there is a calibration process you must follow before flying, which is a minor inconvenience but you learn the routine pretty quickly. The controller has a number of directional buttons but the easiest way to learn is to go outside in a large, clear area and experiment - after about an hour of flight time, you can get very proficient with the joysticks.

The unit broadcasts video back to your phone (or records to the provided SD card) and it's entertaining to watch your flight experience. This is not a stabilized gimbal so don't expect SteadiCam-style gliding - it can get a little rough at times - and there's no audio.

The machine will hover by itself with very little drift, and the return to home button works well. There is an option to use indoors but it's not a great idea - I decapitated a houseplant, nipped on my fingers and almost destroyed a light fixture. Without the GPS (and in the hands of a novice), indoor flying isn't particularly safe.

This drone is a good unit for beginners, older kids and supervised children, and can get you used to the basics of how drone operation works. After a few flights, you'll find yourself wanting to upgrade to something more expensive with more features, but at this price level it's a great way to learn the ropes.

text:
Good quality paint. Iridescently pigmented and lots of mica flake. The flake is fairly fine and spreads evenly in washes. I usually use an eyedropper to dampen paints a moment while I Sketch my design,then paint once the water takes up the pigment and softens it. With these, I do need to take a little extra care mixing on my pallette, and also smooth out the cake of paint in the pan if using it on the brush directly. It handles a bit like a thicker type of paint because of the flake.

I like using them in skies or on water surfaces to add a little extra gleam and luminosity, so I tend to thin them out a good deal and.mix with other colors. They hold up well and blend well without losing their sparkly quality combined with other paints.

I also have the box of various blacks,and experimented mixing these with those on the page and ended up with profoundly 'velvety' luminousity. Like a photo of a velvet dress or curtain. Lovely. I will be buying more of these when they run out, which probably won't be anytime soon... They are large 2cm x 3 xm pans, about half full, for a total of 4-5 mm depthof driet paint. They do not stay sticky like sugar based or gumarabic based binders. The pans are firm and tackless when dry. Would highly recommend.

title: Disappointing
text:
I bought this product because the packaging and reviews promised a gentle, effective addition to my skincare routine, but my experience ended up being a mixed bag. First, the positives: the scent is pleasant without being overpowering, and the texture feels nice going on—light and non-greasy. After a few weeks of use I did notice a slight improvement in overall skin smoothness, and it didn’t strip my skin the way some stronger formulas do.

That said, there are a few disappointments. The results were subtler than I expected from the marketing. I was hoping for more noticeable brightening and reduction in uneven tone, but those changes have been minimal. Also, the pump on my bottle started to stick after about three weeks, which made dispensing messy and frustrating. For the price point I expected better quality control.

I also had a small breakout after introducing the product, although it’s hard to say whether that was caused by this alone since I had a few other variables in my routine. I stopped using it for a week and the irritation subsided; when I reintroduced it slowly, the reaction did not recur, so it may be sensitivity rather than a full incompatibility.

Overall, I think this might work well for someone looking for a gentle, light formula and who doesn’t need dramatic results. It’s not a bad product, but it’s not a miracle worker either, and the packaging durability issues left me underwhelmed. I’m giving it three stars because it’s fine, just not worth repurchasing for me.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I rarely write reviews, but I had to for this one — Opened my EYES! completely changed how I look at my daily life and the choices I make. From the first chapter I felt like the author was speaking directly to me: clear, compassionate, and unafraid to challenge common assumptions. The blend of personal anecdotes and practical exercises made the ideas land in a way that was both emotionally resonant and immediately useful.

What surprised me most was how accessible the writing is. Complex concepts are explained in straightforward language, and the short reflection prompts at the end of each chapter helped me turn insight into action. I started small — just a five-minute breathing practice and a couple of the suggested journal questions — and already noticed a shift in my focus and patience. Several passages made me pause and reconsider long-held habits, and the “reality check” sections were gentle but incisive.

The pacing is excellent; the book moves quickly enough to stay engaging but contains enough depth to be worth revisiting. I also appreciated the resource list at the back — books, apps, and websites that expand on the topics covered. The author’s voice feels trustworthy and grounded, not preachy, which made it easy to accept the tougher suggestions.

After finishing it, I gifted copies to two friends because I genuinely thought they would benefit. If you’re open to looking at your life with a little more clarity and intention, this book is a must-read. Five stars.

If possible, find the Fourth Edition, which includes several amusing additions, in which Wister takes on some of his literary critics.

I have now bought 5 copies of this book, as well as the one I inherited from my father. Buy it, treasure it and pass it along. Some day, I hope, the BBC will make a film version of it. Read it, and see if you agree that Brian Blessed was born to play the Lord of Wantley Manor.

I was pleasantly surprised by this purchase. I ordered it because I needed something functional and reasonably priced, and while it’s not perfect, it’s become a useful part of my daily routine.

It looks better in person than in the product photos — the color is slightly richer and the texture has a subtle sheen that fits well with my other kitchen items. Setup was straightforward; everything that needed to be attached fit together easily without extra tools or guesswork. Instructions were clear and concise, which is always a relief.

Performance-wise it does the job. It handles the expected tasks without fuss and I’ve had no major issues after a month of regular use. It’s relatively quiet in operation and energy use seems reasonable, though I didn’t time or meter it. The capacity is a good middle ground — large enough for my small family needs but not so big that it takes up too much counter or storage space. Cleaning is simpler than I anticipated; most surfaces wipe down easily and a few removable parts are dishwasher-safe, which I appreciate.

Some drawbacks kept me from giving this five stars. The manual could use more troubleshooting tips — a few common questions (like how to reset or deal with minor jams) aren’t addressed. One small plastic clip creaked after a couple of uses, and while it still functions, the noise is noticeable. Also, while the product matches the advertised dimensions closely, the fit in a narrow cabinet is snugger than I expected; if you have tight storage, double-check measurements before buying.

Customer support was responsive when I emailed with a question about replacement parts. The reply came within 48 hours and included helpful links and clear next steps, which was reassuring.

Overall, this product delivers excellent value. It balances design, performance, and price well. If you want something reliable for everyday use without spending a lot, this is worth considering. Just keep an eye on the small clip area and be sure it will fit in your intended storage spot. I’d buy it again.

It can be dimmed for use as a fill or backlight. However, because it is a panel of lights, it cannot be used as a focused spotlight. The panel cover is a diffuser that softens the light considerably. Overall I would say this is a terrific light and worth the price. Easily 5 stars.

On the plus side, the applicator is comfortable to hold and the product initially went on smoothly, blending well without tugging. The scent is mild and not bothersome, which I appreciate since I'm sensitive to strong fragrances. Packaging feels pretty and could work as a gift if it held up longer.

It also doesn't tolerate a little splashing—if you drip a bit of soapy water on the surface it streaks and becomes blotchy, and I had to be careful where I set it in my bathroom. Performance-wise the formula is okay but not outstanding; it lasts through a normal workday but starts to fade towards the evening, and I found myself reapplying more than I'd like.

I’d recommend this to anyone looking for a thoughtful gift for a preteen who likes hands-on activities. It’s fun, educational, and sturdy — exactly what I hoped for.

If you’re looking for an affordable, attractive accent that pays homage to Sioux motifs without feeling kitschy, this is a great choice. It’s well-made, visually appealing, and adds character to the room. Highly recommend for anyone furnishing a themed space or just wanting a distinctive piece with a rustic, Southwestern vibe.

If you’re comfortable with a little initial tweaking and getting used to the mouse control, this product is a great value. title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I’ve been using these for a few weeks after deciding to switch from my old gel pens to something the office kept recommending. There are definitely pros and cons, which is why I’m giving three stars.

On the plus side, the pens look and feel professional. The barrel is solidly built and has a pleasant weight — not too light, not too heavy — so they don’t feel cheap when you hand them out in meetings. The ink dries faster than my previous pens, which is great for left-handed notes and reduces smudging. The lines are consistent at a medium thickness; good for everyday note-taking, signing documents, and printing charts. The black ink is a true black and photocopies clearly without ghosting.

However, the experience isn’t flawless. First, the grip section is slightly slippery. If you tend to write for long stretches, your fingers start to feel a bit tired because there isn’t much cushioning. Second, a few of the pens in the pack (about 2 out of 12) started to feel scratchy after a couple of weeks, like the tip wasn’t as smooth as the others. They still write, but the feel is noticeably different and a little annoying. Also, while the ink dries faster than my old pens, it still smears a little on cheaper paper stock — not a dealbreaker, but something to be aware of if you frequently use lower-quality notebooks or thermal paper.

Refill availability is another concern. The product description hinted at long-lasting cartridges, but the pens don’t appear to be easily refillable, and I couldn’t find compatible refills locally. If you plan to use these heavily, be prepared to replace the entire pen instead of just swapping a cartridge.

Overall, these pens are solid for everyday office use: they look professional, write cleanly, and mostly avoid smudging. But the inconsistent tip quality in my pack, the slippery grip, and uncertain refill options mean they’re not perfect. If you want a reliable, mid-range pen for occasional to moderate use, these are a fine choice. If you’re looking for something with an ergonomic grip or long-term refillable convenience, you might want to keep looking.

If you want comfortable, reliable ear hooks with elastic straps that actually make wearing earbuds for long periods pleasant, these are a great buy. title: Original fantasy with strong world building and characters
text:
Full disclosure: I won this in a Goodreads giveaway.

It's very, very rare to come across a truly original entry in the epic fantasy world, these days. Though in some ways I'm not even sure fantasy describes this book. Yes, it's obviously fantasy with magic and different races and such things, but at the same time it doesn't seem to focus on those things. It doesn't have the 'feel' of a typical fantasy book, and to me that's a good thing. Perhaps because it lacks some of the heaviness that many serious fantasy novels have. I did find that to be a good thing, though. It let the story move fairly quickly without getting bogged down on small details.

The world itself is very well laid out, especially because the reader is discovering it as the main character does. Rather clever of the author, there. Didn't even occur to me as I was reading, but in retrospect it worked and was very entertaining.

Characters...complex, interesting, well-rounded. I could go on, but you get the idea. At no point did I get the feeling I was dealing with cut outs or your typical fantasy cliches. Though I'll admit I'm a sucker for an anti-hero, which the main character definitely is. The relationships throughout the story are just as interesting, and nothing is ever quite as it seems.

I found the story itself to be very compelling and very original. It was one of those books that I couldn't wait to pick up when I had to set it down to go do something else. Halfway through I found myself lamenting the fact that there aren't any other books in the series written yet. I'm not going to talk much about it because there really is a lot to give away. I, for one, did not see the twists coming.

I really look forward to the next book in the series and finding out more about these characters, as well as the world they live in. Unlike so many books, these days, there's a very satisfying ending to this tale. Yes, it's apparently part of a larger story arc, but the author has not neglected the necessary resolution in each smaller part.

title: Fits my Mosin Nagant 91/30
text:
I bought this sling hoping it would be an affordable, authentic-feeling replacement for the tired, cracked leather piece on my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and it exceeded my expectations. Right out of the package the quality was obvious — the leather has a nice, solid feel without being overly stiff, and the stitching looks durable and well-done. Installation was straightforward; the hardware lined up with the rifle’s original fittings and I had it mounted and adjusted in less than ten minutes.

Fit is excellent. The length and buckle placement are right where they should be for the Mosin Nagant 91/30, allowing me to carry the rifle comfortably for extended periods and to bring it to the shoulder quickly without fumbling. The sling holds the rifle securely when slung and doesn’t slip under load. The leather softened a bit with rubbing-in and now conforms to my body nicely.

Functionally it performs exactly as advertised — a dependable field sling that feels period-appropriate. Aesthetically it complements the rifle well; the color and finish match the vintage look of my Mosin. After a couple of range sessions and a few walks in the woods, there’s only mild, attractive patina developing.

If I have one nitpick it’s that the edge finish could be slightly smoother, but that’s purely cosmetic and hasn’t affected performance. Overall I’m very pleased — great value for the price and a perfect fit for the 91/30. If you’re looking for a solid replacement sling that’s ready to use out of the box, this one is a great choice. Five stars.

title: I recommend this book to any one who is interested in organizing their contacts!
text:
I bought this book because my contact list had become a disorganized mess—names without context, old numbers, duplicate entries across phone, email, and social media. I wasn’t expecting a miracle, just something practical. What I got was far better: clear, actionable guidance that I could apply immediately.

The author breaks the process into manageable steps: auditing current contacts, deciding what to keep, consolidating duplicates, and adding meaningful tags or notes so each entry is useful. I appreciated the balance between big-picture principles (like why maintaining relationships matters) and nitty-gritty tactics (how to export and merge lists, best practices for naming conventions, and templates for brief outreach messages). The examples felt realistic and not overly technical, which made them easy to follow even though I’m not tech-savvy.

I followed the recommended 90-minute audit and was able to streamline hundreds of entries into a clean, searchable list. The section on maintaining momentum—simple weekly habits to keep the list current—has been a game-changer. My follow-up outreach felt more personal because I had context at my fingertips.

If you want to stop wasting time hunting for contact details and start using your network more intentionally, this book is worth it. Practical, friendly, and full of useful templates and checklists—exactly what someone trying to get organized needs.
